Slice: Place Hold

Step 1 of 29 in Hold a tool for pickup · the story starts here · before My Holds · State Change

Intent

Let a neighbor get in line for a tool that isn't available to borrow right now, by placing a hold from the Tool Catalog. Holds on a tool are fulfilled in the order they were placed: when the tool is back in the shed, it is set aside for the neighbor at the front of the queue.

Trigger & Actor

A neighbor, from the Tool Catalog, on a tool that is checked out, set aside for a holder, or reserved (back in the shed with holds waiting, not yet set aside). The catalog is the same for every neighbor, so it offers Place Hold on every such tool to everyone; a neighbor who may not hold it is refused with a reason they can see. The shed manager doesn't place holds.

Command / Input

Command: Place Hold

A HoldId, ToolId or NeighborId is a UUID.

FieldTypeRequiredRules / Validation
holdIdHoldIdyesA UUID chosen by the caller for the new hold, so a retried request is recognised. Must not belong to a different hold already placed (INV-HOLD-13).
toolIdToolIdyesThe tool to hold. Must be a tool that has been added (INV-HOLD-14), not retired (INV-HOLD-3), and not available (INV-HOLD-2).
neighborIdNeighborIdyesThe neighbor placing the hold, who must be the one making the request (INV-HOLD-1). Must be a registered account (INV-HOLD-14), not closed (INV-HOLD-4) and not suspended (INV-HOLD-9).

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Tool Catalog @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Hold Placed → context Holds Read by: My Holds (its own slice, which shows the neighbor their place in the queue), Tool Catalog (holds waiting, and a tool's status), My Loans (a hold waiting on a borrowed tool), and Holds To Fulfill (the queue the hold fulfiller works from).

FieldTypeImmutable Fact?Source / Notes
holdIdHoldIdyesFrom the command. Identifies the hold everywhere from here on.
toolIdToolIdyesFrom the command.
toolNameTextyesSet by the system: the tool's name as recorded by Tool Added, copied so the hold's readers never look it up.
neighborIdNeighborIdyesFrom the command: the holder.
neighborNameTextyesSet by the system: the holder's name as recorded by Neighbor Registered.
neighborEmailTextyesSet by the system: the holder's email current when the hold is placed (Neighbor Registered, replaced by any Neighbor Email Changed).
placedAtInstantyesThe UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system. For display only: the queue is the order Hold Placed is recorded, since two holds can share a timestamp.

Every field is fixed for good. A hold's later life (fulfilled, cancelled, expired, ended) is recorded by other events; nothing changes Hold Placed.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Hold Placed feeds four views, each specified in its own doc:

  • My Holds (slices/my-holds.md) shows the neighbor the new hold and its place in the queue.
  • Tool Catalog (slices/tool-catalog.md) counts it among the holds waiting on the tool.
  • My Loans (slices/my-loans.md) shows the borrower of the tool that someone is waiting.
  • Holds To Fulfill (slices/holds-to-fulfill.md) adds it to the tool's queue.

All are eventually consistent: the hold shows once each view has caught up with Hold Placed.

Invariants / Business Rules

A tool's state, for these rules, is tested against its events as already recorded, in this order; the first that holds wins:

  1. checked-out — a loan of the tool is open: Tool Checked Out recorded, and neither Tool Returned nor Tool Lost for that loan.
  2. set-aside — otherwise, a hold on the tool has been fulfilled and hasn't ended.
  3. reserved — otherwise, at least one hold on the tool is waiting.
  4. available — otherwise.

This is the same test the Tool Catalog uses for a tool's status.

A hold is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, when the holder checks the tool out, when the tool is retired or recorded lost, or when the holder closes their account. Once fulfilled, the tool is set aside for the holder until the end of the collect-by date, the set-aside date plus 3 days; a set-aside whose collect-by date has passed still counts as set aside until Hold Expired is recorded for it. Other slices record these endings; this slice reads them.

The Tool Catalog is the same for every neighbor, so it offers Place Hold on every tool that isn't available and can't hide the action from a neighbor who may not use it. Each rule below that refuses a neighbor (INV-HOLD-4, INV-HOLD-7, INV-HOLD-8, INV-HOLD-9) does so with a reason the neighbor can see.

  • INV-HOLD-1: A neighbor places a hold themselves, from the Tool Catalog, and only for themselves.
    • The neighbor ID must be the neighbor making the request. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch.
  • INV-HOLD-2: A hold can be placed on any tool that isn't available.
    • That is a tool that is checked out, set aside for a holder, or back in the shed with holds waiting but not yet set aside.
    • A hold on an available tool is refused. The neighbor checks it out instead.
  • INV-HOLD-3: A hold can't be placed on a retired tool.
    • A tool recorded lost is retired by that. Retiring a tool ends every hold on it.
  • INV-HOLD-4: A neighbor whose account is closed can't place a hold.
    • Closing an account ends all of that neighbor's holds.
  • INV-HOLD-5: A new hold joins the back of the tool's queue.
    • The order is the order Hold Placed events are recorded for the tool. placedAt is for display only, since two holds can share a timestamp. Holds on one tool are decided one at a time, so no two share a place.
    • Holds are fulfilled in queue order; that is Fulfill Hold's rule (INV-FUL-2).
  • INV-HOLD-7: A neighbor can have only one hold on a given tool.
    • A second hold by the same neighbor on the same tool is refused, whether their first hold is waiting or set aside.
    • A hold that has ended doesn't count. After cancelling, or once their hold has expired, the neighbor may hold the tool again, at the back of the queue.
  • INV-HOLD-8: A neighbor can't place a hold on a tool they have on loan themselves.
  • INV-HOLD-9: A suspended neighbor can't place a new hold.
    • Holds they placed before the suspension keep their place in the queue.
  • INV-HOLD-10: A neighbor with an overdue loan may place a hold.
    • The overdue loan stops them collecting the tool if it is set aside for them (Check Out Tool, INV-CHK-5), not placing the hold.
  • INV-HOLD-11: There is no limit on how many holds one neighbor can have at once.
  • INV-HOLD-13: Placing a hold with a hold ID that is already used places no new hold.
    • A repeat with the same tool and neighbor succeeds and records nothing new, whatever has happened to the hold since. A repeat with a different tool or neighbor is refused (hold-id-in-use).
  • INV-HOLD-14: The tool must have been added, and the neighbor must be a registered account.
  • INV-HOLD-15: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path: first hold on a checked-out tool (INV-HOLD-2, INV-HOLD-5)
    • Given: Ana (N1) has the cordless drill (T1) on loan, due 12 October, and no holds are waiting on it. Ben (N2) is active.
    • When: Ben places hold H1 on T1 from the Tool Catalog
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H1: T1, N2, and the time it was placed.
  • Second hold queues behind the first (INV-HOLD-5)
    • Given: T1 is checked out, and Ben's hold H1 on it is waiting
    • When: Cleo (N3) places hold H2 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H2, after H1. H2 is behind H1 in T1's queue.
  • Hold on a set-aside tool (INV-HOLD-2)
    • Given: T1 was returned and is set aside for Ben's hold H1, and no other hold is waiting
    • When: Cleo places hold H2 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H2, behind Ben's set-aside.
  • Hold on a reserved tool (INV-HOLD-2)
    • Given: T1 has just been returned, Ben's hold H1 is waiting, and Hold Fulfilled has not yet been recorded
    • When: Cleo places hold H2 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H2, behind H1.
  • Available tool (INV-HOLD-2)
    • Given: the ladder (T2) is in the shed with no holds
    • When: Ben tries to place a hold on T2
    • Then: refused with tool-available: "This tool is available. Check it out instead." No event is recorded.
  • Retired tool (INV-HOLD-3)
    • Given: T1 was retired while Ana had it on loan
    • When: Ben tries to place a hold on T1
    • Then: refused with tool-retired: "This tool has been retired." No event is recorded.
  • Already holding this tool (INV-HOLD-7)
    • Given: T1 is checked out, and Ben's hold H1 on it is waiting
    • When: Ben tries to place hold H3 on T1
    • Then: refused with already-holding: "You already have a hold on this tool." No event is recorded.
  • Already holding this tool, set aside for them (INV-HOLD-7)
    • Given: T1 is set aside for Ben's hold H1
    • When: Ben tries to place hold H3 on T1
    • Then: refused with already-holding: "You already have a hold on this tool." No event is recorded.
  • Holding again after cancelling (INV-HOLD-7)
    • Given: T1 is checked out, Ben's hold H1 on it was cancelled, and Cleo's hold H2 is waiting
    • When: Ben places hold H4 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H4, behind H2.
  • Holding again after expiry (INV-HOLD-7)
    • Given: T1 was set aside for Ben's hold H1, Hold Expired was recorded for H1, and Cleo now has T1 on loan
    • When: Ben places hold H5 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H5.
  • Tool on loan to the neighbor (INV-HOLD-8)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan
    • When: Ana tries to place a hold on T1
    • Then: refused with tool-on-loan-to-you: "You have this tool on loan." No event is recorded.
  • Suspended neighbor (INV-HOLD-9)
    • Given: T1 is checked out by Ana, and Ben is suspended
    • When: Ben tries to place a hold on T1
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended: "You can't place holds while your account is suspended." No event is recorded.
  • Closed account (INV-HOLD-4)
    • Given: T1 is checked out by Ana, and Ben's account is closed
    • When: a hold on T1 is requested for Ben
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." No event is recorded.
  • Neighbor with an overdue loan (INV-HOLD-10)
    • Given: Ben has the ladder on loan, overdue, and Ana has T1 on loan
    • When: Ben places hold H6 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H6.
  • Holds on several tools (INV-HOLD-11)
    • Given: Ben's hold H1 on T1 is waiting, and the hedge trimmer (T3) is checked out by Ana
    • When: Ben places hold H7 on T3
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H7. Ben now has holds on T1 and T3.
  • A hold for someone else (INV-HOLD-1)
    • Given: T1 is checked out by Ana
    • When: a request from Ben asks to place a hold on T1 for Cleo
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only place holds for yourself." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown tool (INV-HOLD-14)
    • Given: no tool has ID T9
    • When: Ben asks to place a hold on T9
    • Then: refused with tool-not-found: "There is no such tool." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown neighbor (INV-HOLD-14)
    • Given: T1 is checked out by Ana, and no account has neighbor ID N9
    • When: a hold on T1 is requested for N9
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.
  • Hold on a lapsed set-aside (INV-HOLD-2)
    • Given: T1 was set aside for Ben's hold H1, collect by 17 October, and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded for H1
    • When: on 18 October, Cleo places hold H8 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H8. T1 still counts as set aside, not available.
  • Lapsed holder holds again before expiry (INV-HOLD-7)
    • Given: T1 was set aside for Ben's hold H1, collect by 17 October, and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded for H1
    • When: on 18 October, Ben tries to place hold H9 on T1
    • Then: refused with already-holding: "You already have a hold on this tool." No event is recorded. Once Hold Expired is recorded for H1, he may hold T1 again.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-HOLD-13)
    • Given: Hold Placed was recorded for H1: T1, Ben
    • When: the same Place Hold request for H1, T1, Ben arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. Ben still has one hold on T1.
  • The same request after the hold ended (INV-HOLD-13)
    • Given: Hold Placed was recorded for H1: T1, Ben, and H1 has since been cancelled
    • When: the same Place Hold request for H1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. H1 stays cancelled.
  • A hold ID reused for a different hold (INV-HOLD-13)
    • Given: Hold Placed was recorded for H1: T1, Ben
    • When: a Place Hold request arrives for H1 with T3, Ben
    • Then: refused with hold-id-in-use: "That hold ID is already used by another hold." No event is recorded.
  • Not signed in (INV-HOLD-15)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: a request for placing a hold arrives
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the neighbor on the Tool Catalog screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-HOLD-15): a request with no sign-in is refused first.
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-HOLD-1): who is asking is settled next, before any other rule.
  3. The hold ID is already used (INV-HOLD-13): a repeat with the same details succeeds with nothing recorded; otherwise hold-id-in-use.
  4. tool-not-found, then neighbor-not-found (INV-HOLD-14).
  5. tool-retired (INV-HOLD-3).
  6. account-closed, then neighbor-suspended (INV-HOLD-4, INV-HOLD-9).
  7. tool-on-loan-to-you (INV-HOLD-8).
  8. already-holding (INV-HOLD-7).
  9. tool-available (INV-HOLD-2).
ReasonSentenceRule
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-HOLD-15
hold-id-in-useThat hold ID is already used by another hold.INV-HOLD-13
requester-mismatchYou can only place holds for yourself.INV-HOLD-1
tool-not-foundThere is no such tool.INV-HOLD-14
neighbor-not-foundThere is no such neighbor.INV-HOLD-14
tool-retiredThis tool has been retired.INV-HOLD-3
account-closedThis account is closed.INV-HOLD-4
neighbor-suspendedYou can't place holds while your account is suspended.INV-HOLD-9
tool-on-loan-to-youYou have this tool on loan.INV-HOLD-8
already-holdingYou already have a hold on this tool.INV-HOLD-7
tool-availableThis tool is available. Check it out instead.INV-HOLD-2

hold-id-in-use, tool-not-found and neighbor-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name. The names and sentences shared with Check Out Tool (tool-not-found, neighbor-not-found, tool-retired, account-closed) are worded the same there.

Idempotency: a repeated request with the same hold ID, tool and neighbor succeeds and records nothing new, even if the hold has since been fulfilled, cancelled, expired or ended. So a retry after a lost response never places a second hold.

Requests at the same moment: each Place Hold is decided against the tool's holds and loans as already recorded, one at a time per tool. Two neighbors holding the same tool together are both recorded, in the order they are decided. The same neighbor sending two holds on one tool together gets one recorded; the other is refused with already-holding.

A set-aside past its collect-by date still counts as set aside until Hold Expired is recorded for it. Until then the tool is not available, so a hold on it is accepted (INV-HOLD-2), and the lapsed holder's own hold still counts as theirs (INV-HOLD-7).

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice. Placing a hold sends no email.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may place a hold only for themselves (INV-HOLD-1); the shed manager doesn't place holds. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch.
  • PII & compliance: Hold Placed links a neighbor to a tool. It holds no name or email; those stay on Neighbor Registered and Neighbor Email Changed.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time rule above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Hold Placed (this slice): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These keys match slices/add-tool.md, slices/register-neighbor.md, slices/check-out-tool.md, slices/tool-inventory.md and slices/tool-catalog.md. The others are specified in slices not yet written in depth; each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans and Holds To Fulfill (the new hold). Fulfill Hold sets the tool aside for the front of the queue; Cancel Hold, Expire Hold, Check Out Tool, Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost and Close Account end holds; Extend Loan refuses while a hold is waiting.

Open Questions

None.

State Viewv2DraftDelta pending

Slice: My Holds

Step 2 of 29 in Hold a tool for pickup · after Place Hold · before Tool Catalog — hold placed · State View

Intent

Shows a neighbor the holds they have, on the My Holds screen: where they stand in each tool's queue, and when a tool has been set aside for them, the date to collect it by and whether the pickup email reached them. It is the only screen that tells a neighbor a tool is waiting for them, and the screen they cancel holds from.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: a neighbor, opening their own My Holds screen.
  • Whose holds it shows: the holds of the neighbor asking. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the neighbor's ID, resolving a person to their newest account, or to their closed one only when they have no newer.
  • Actions offered: nothing on this screen records anything by itself. Its one action issues a command owned by another slice:
    • Cancel (Cancel Hold slice) — offered on every listed hold (INV-MYHD-16).
    • A neighbor collects a set-aside tool with an ordinary checkout from the Tool Catalog, not from here.

Read Model / View

  • View: My Holds built from events: "Hold Placed", "Hold Collected", "Hold Cancelled", "Hold Fulfilled", "Pickup Notice Sent", "Pickup Notice Failed", "Hold Expired"
  • Consumed by: the My Holds screen (Neighbor)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events: a change shows shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Whether a set-aside's pickup window has ended is worked out when the view is read, from collectByDate and today's date in the shed's local time zone, so it is always current. No action on this screen depends on the view being instant, because Cancel Hold and Check Out Tool each check their own rules when they run.

One row per hold that hasn't ended. HoldId, ToolId, LoanId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be absent.

FieldTypeSource / Notes
holdIdHoldIdHold Placed.holdId.
neighborIdNeighborIdHold Placed.neighborId: the holder.
toolIdToolIdHold Placed.toolId.
toolNameTextHold Placed.toolName (INV-MYHD-14).
placedAtInstantHold Placed.placedAt. For display only; it doesn't decide the queue.
statusTextOne of waiting, ready-for-pickup, pickup-window-ended. Derived: see the status rules below.
positionIntDerived: while status is waiting, 1 plus the number of this tool's holds that are waiting, were placed before this one, and haven't ended (INV-MYHD-2). Optional: absent once the hold is fulfilled.
collectByDateDateDerived: Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate for this hold, read as recorded, never worked out here (INV-MYHD-3). Optional: absent while waiting.
pickupNoticeTextOne of none, sent, undelivered. Derived: sent once Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for this hold, undelivered once Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for it, none before either (INV-MYHD-13).
canCancelBoolDerived: yes on every listed hold (INV-MYHD-16).

Status rules. A hold's status is a test of its current facts, taken in this order. The first that holds wins:

  1. pickup-window-ended — Hold Fulfilled has been recorded for the hold, and today's date in the shed's local time zone is after its collectByDate (INV-MYHD-17).
  2. ready-for-pickup — otherwise, Hold Fulfilled has been recorded for the hold.
  3. waiting — otherwise.

When a hold leaves the view. A hold is listed from Hold Placed until it ends. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, or when the holder checks the tool out. In events:

  • Hold Cancelled or Hold Expired for the hold;
  • Hold Collected for the hold (the holder checked the tool out).

Retiring the tool, recording it lost and closing the holder's account each end holds by recording Hold Cancelled for them (Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost, Close Account). This view hears only the Holds events.

Queue order. A tool's queue is the order in which Hold Placed was recorded for it. To work out positions, the view keeps, for each tool, every hold on it that hasn't ended, with its holder and whether it has been fulfilled. This is bookkeeping, not part of the row, and other neighbors' holds are never returned.

Queries

  • List my holds. Takes the asking neighbor's neighborId. Returns every hold of that neighbor that hasn't ended, each with every field above, and nothing about anyone else's holds (INV-MYHD-1). There is no paging. A neighbor with no holds gets an empty list. Holds are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when the hold was placed, in the order Hold Placed was recorded (INV-MYHD-18).

Invariants / Business Rules

A neighbor has at most one hold on any one tool, because Place Hold refuses a second (INV-HOLD-7, Place Hold). A suspended neighbor can't place a new hold (INV-HOLD-9) or collect a set-aside tool (INV-CHK-7), but may still cancel. An expired hold sends no message, doesn't count against the neighbor, and the neighbor may place a new hold on the tool at the back of the queue (Expire Hold). A suspended neighbor keeps their holds and their place in each queue. A front holder who can't collect, because they are suspended or have an overdue loan, still has the tool set aside for them, and the pickup window runs regardless (Fulfill Hold, INV-FUL-8). These rules are owned by those slices; this view just reflects the events they record, and it doesn't hear suspension or loans at all (INV-MYHD-11).

  • INV-MYHD-1: A neighbor's My Holds shows only their own holds.
    • The query returns only holds whose holder is the neighbor ID it is given. It never shows who else holds a tool, only the neighbor's own position. No neighbor-facing screen ever shows who has a tool or who holds one; only the shed manager sees borrowers, on Tool Inventory.
  • INV-MYHD-2: Holds on a tool queue in the order they were placed. Each waiting hold shows the neighbor's position in that tool's queue.
    • Position 1 is the next hold to be fulfilled. A hold moves up as holds ahead of it are fulfilled or end.
    • A hold that has been fulfilled is no longer in the waiting queue, so the first waiting hold behind a set-aside is at position 1.
  • INV-MYHD-3: Once a neighbor's hold is fulfilled, My Holds shows the tool as ready for pickup, with the date to collect it by.
    • The collect-by date is the one Hold Fulfilled carries: the date the tool was set aside plus 3 days. My Holds shows it as recorded and never works it out itself.
    • My Holds is the only screen that tells a neighbor a tool is set aside for them. The Tool Catalog is the same for every neighbor.
  • INV-MYHD-4: A hold that is ready for pickup stays on My Holds until the holder collects it, cancels it, or Hold Expired is recorded for it. Then it drops off.
    • The tool then passes to the next hold, which shows as ready for pickup on that neighbor's My Holds once Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • INV-MYHD-5: When a holder checks out the tool they hold, their hold ends and drops off My Holds, whether or not it had been fulfilled.
    • The loan then appears on My Loans.
  • INV-MYHD-6: A cancelled hold drops off My Holds, whether it was waiting or ready for pickup.
    • Cancelling a hold that is ready for pickup passes the tool to the next hold, the same as expiry.
  • INV-MYHD-7: Retiring a tool, or recording it lost, ends every hold on it, and those holds drop off My Holds.
    • Retire Tool and Record Tool Lost record Hold Cancelled for each hold; this view hears those. The holders are not told.
  • INV-MYHD-8: Closing an account ends all of that neighbor's holds. Their holds drop off My Holds, and holds behind them move up.
    • Close Account records Hold Cancelled for each of the neighbor's holds; this view hears those.
    • A tool that was ready for pickup for them passes to the next hold, the same as expiry.
  • INV-MYHD-13: Once a tool is set aside for a neighbor, My Holds shows whether the pickup email was sent or couldn't be delivered.
    • If the email can't be delivered, the tool stays ready for pickup, with the same collect-by date.
  • INV-MYHD-14: Each hold shows the tool's name.
    • The name comes with Hold Placed, which carries it.
  • INV-MYHD-11: Only Hold Placed, Hold Collected, Hold Cancelled, Hold Fulfilled, Pickup Notice Sent, Pickup Notice Failed and Hold Expired change My Holds.
    • A checkout records Hold Collected only when the borrower had a hold on the tool; a checkout by anyone else is not heard here at all.
  • INV-MYHD-15: Applying the same event twice leaves My Holds as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-MYHD-16: My Holds offers Cancel on every hold it lists.
    • That includes holds ready for pickup, holds whose pickup window has ended, and holds of a suspended neighbor.
  • INV-MYHD-17: Once a set-aside's collect-by date has passed, My Holds shows that the pickup window has ended, even before Hold Expired is recorded.
    • From the start of the day after the collect-by date, in the shed's local time, the set-aside is no longer theirs: the tool goes to the next neighbor in the queue, or to whoever checks it out first if nobody is waiting (INV-CHK-3b, Check Out Tool). The hold drops off when Hold Expired is recorded.
  • INV-MYHD-18: Holds are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when they were placed.
  • INV-MYHD-19: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.
  • INV-MYHD-20: My Holds is answered only for the signed-in neighbor: a request for any other neighbor ID is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Hold placed (INV-MYHD-2, INV-MYHD-14, INV-MYHD-16)
    • Given: Ana has T1, the "Cordless drill", on loan, and nobody has a hold on it
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's hold H1 on T1, carrying the name "Cordless drill"
    • Then: Ben's My Holds lists H1: "Cordless drill", waiting, position 1, pickup notice none, with Cancel offered.
  • A second hold placed (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Cara's hold H2 on T1
    • Then: Cara's My Holds lists H2, waiting, position 2. Ben's is unchanged.
  • Holds placed in the same instant (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Cara's H2 and then Dan's H3 on T1, with the same placedAt
    • Then: H2 is at position 2 and H3 at position 3: the order recorded decides, not placedAt.
  • Hold cancelled (INV-MYHD-6, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Hold fulfilled (INV-MYHD-3, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1, and T1 has been returned
    • When: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1, with the collect-by date 17 October
    • Then: Ben's My Holds shows H1 ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, with no position. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Pickup email sent (INV-MYHD-13)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, pickup notice none
    • When: Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 shows pickup notice sent.
  • Pickup email couldn't be delivered (INV-MYHD-13)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, pickup notice sent
    • When: Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 shows pickup notice undelivered, still ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October.
  • Collect-by date is the last day (INV-MYHD-17)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October
    • When: his holds are listed at 23:59 on 17 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 is ready-for-pickup.
  • Pickup window ended, not yet expired (INV-MYHD-17, INV-MYHD-16)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded
    • When: his holds are listed at 00:00 on 18 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 shows pickup-window-ended, with Cancel still offered.
  • Hold expired (INV-MYHD-4)
    • Given: Ben's H1 shows pickup-window-ended, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 stays waiting at position 1 until Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • Suspended holder (INV-MYHD-3, INV-MYHD-11)
    • Given: Ben is suspended, and his H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: T1 is returned and Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1, collect by 17 October
    • Then: Ben's My Holds shows H1 ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October.
  • Holder collects the tool (INV-MYHD-5)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Collected is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's is unchanged.
  • Front holder collects before the set-aside is recorded (INV-MYHD-5, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1, and T1 has just been returned
    • When: Hold Collected is recorded for H1, before any Hold Fulfilled
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Ready-for-pickup hold cancelled (INV-MYHD-6)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 stays waiting until Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • Tool retired (INV-MYHD-7)
    • Given: Ben's H1 and Cara's H2 are on T1
    • When: Retire Tool records Hold Cancelled for H1 and for H2, with Tool Retired for T1
    • Then: H1 and H2 drop off both neighbors' My Holds.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-MYHD-7)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan as loan L1, and Ben's H1 and Cara's H2 are on T1
    • When: Record Tool Lost records Hold Cancelled for H1 and for H2, with Tool Lost for L1
    • Then: H1 and H2 drop off both neighbors' My Holds.
  • Holder closes their account (INV-MYHD-8)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1
    • When: Close Account records Hold Cancelled for H1, with Neighbor Account Closed for Ben
    • Then: H1 drops off. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Hold again after expiry (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 expired, and T1 is now set aside for Cara's H2
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's new hold H4 on T1
    • Then: Ben's My Holds lists H4, waiting, position 1, behind Cara's set-aside.
  • Only their own holds (INV-MYHD-1)
    • Given: Ben has H1 and Cara has H2, both on T1
    • When: Ben's holds are listed
    • Then: only H1 is returned, with its position. Nothing about H2 or Cara is returned.
  • List order (INV-MYHD-18)
    • Given: Ben placed H5 on the ladder, then H1 on the cordless drill
    • When: his holds are listed
    • Then: H1 (cordless drill) comes first, then H5 (ladder).
  • Same event applied twice (INV-MYHD-15)
    • Given: Ben's My Holds lists H1 at position 1
    • When: the same Hold Placed for H1 is applied again
    • Then: Ben's My Holds still lists H1 once, at position 1, and no later hold's position changes.
  • Not signed in (INV-MYHD-19)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: My Holds is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.
  • Asked by the wrong person (INV-MYHD-20)
    • Given: Ben (N2) is signed in
    • When: the holds of N1, Ana, are asked for
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only see your own holds." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

Reading this view is guarded like a command. A refused read returns nothing and one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown on the screen. The checks run in this order:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-MYHD-19).
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-MYHD-20).
ReasonSentenceRule
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-MYHD-19
requester-mismatchYou can only see your own holds.INV-MYHD-20
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-MYHD-15). An event applied a second time leaves the view as it was after the first.
  • Events for a hold that has ended: once a hold has ended it is gone from this view. A later event for it (a replay, or a Pickup Notice Failed that arrives after the set-aside ended) changes nothing.
  • Stale actions: Cancel offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, just as the hold expires or the tool is collected). Cancel Hold checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may list only their own holds (INV-MYHD-1). The query is always asked for the signed-in neighbor's own ID, which sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies; a request for any other neighbor ID is refused requester-mismatch (INV-MYHD-20), and one with no sign-in not-signed-in (INV-MYHD-19).
  • PII & compliance: shows a neighbor their own holds only, and never who else holds or has a tool. The other holders and borrowers it keeps for working out positions are never returned.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId, placedAt.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, collectByDate.
    • Pickup Notice Sent (Send Pickup Notice): holdId.
    • Pickup Notice Failed (Record Pickup Notice Failure): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Collected (Collect Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Cancelled is also recorded by Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost and Close Account, one per hold they end; this view can't tell those from a holder's own cancellation and needn't.
    • Hold Placed and Hold Collected match slices/place-hold.md and slices/check-out-tool.md. The others are specified in slices not yet written in depth; these keys are this view's assumptions, and each is checked when that slice is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Cancel Hold.

Open Questions

None.

Slice: Holds To Collect

Step 5 of 29 in Hold a tool for pickup · after My Loans — hold placed · before Collect Hold · State View

Intent

The hold collector's to-do list: every hold whose holder has checked the tool out and whose hold hasn't yet been recorded collected. The collector works through it, so a holder's own checkout ends their hold as a Holds fact (Hold Collected) and the views about holds never infer it from the loan.

Trigger & Actor

  • Consumed by: the Hold Collector (Collect Hold). Internal: no ui.
  • What it lists: one row per hold that is live (placed, not cancelled, expired or collected) on a tool that its holder now has on loan. A row names the hold, its tool and holder, and the loan that collected it.

Read Model / View

  • View: Holds To Collect built from events: "Hold Placed", "Tool Checked Out", "Hold Collected", "Hold Cancelled"
  • Consumed by: the Hold Collector (Collect Hold). Internal: no ui.
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. A row appears shortly after the checkout is recorded and leaves shortly after Hold Collected is (seconds, not minutes).

HoldId, ToolId, NeighborId and LoanId are UUIDs.

FieldTypeSource / Notes
holdIdHoldIdHold Placed.holdId.
toolIdToolIdHold Placed.toolId.
neighborIdNeighborIdHold Placed.neighborId: the holder.
loanIdLoanIdDerived: Tool Checked Out.loanId of the holder's open loan on the tool.

When a row appears. Tool Checked Out for a tool and neighbor who has a live hold on that tool creates the row for that hold (INV-HTC-1). A holder has at most one hold on a tool (INV-HOLD-2, Place Hold), so the checkout names at most one hold.

When a row leaves. Hold Collected for the hold (INV-HTC-2), or Hold Cancelled for it (INV-HTC-3): a hold cancelled in the moment between the checkout and the collector acting is never collected. Nothing puts a row back.

To know which holds are live, the view keeps, beyond its rows, every hold from Hold Placed until Hold Cancelled or Hold Collected for it. A hold that expired, or ended with its tool retired or lost, cannot be checked out by its holder (INV-CHK-3b, INV-CHK-4), so those endings need no rule here.

Queries

  • List holds to collect. Takes nothing. Returns every row with all four fields. There is no paging. The order doesn't matter to the collector.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-HTC-1: A hold joins the list when its holder's checkout of the tool is recorded.
    • Whether the hold was set aside (INV-CHK-3) or taken from the front of the queue before the set-aside was recorded (INV-CHK-3a) makes no difference: both are collections.
    • A checkout by a neighbor with no live hold on the tool adds nothing.
  • INV-HTC-2: Once Hold Collected is recorded for a hold, it leaves the list and never returns.
  • INV-HTC-3: A hold cancelled before it is collected leaves the list.
  • INV-HTC-4: Applying the same event twice leaves the list as if it had been applied once.

The list has no screen; only the Hold Collector reads it.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ben's hold H1 is live on the cordless drill (T1).

  • Holder collects a set-aside (INV-HTC-1)
    • Given: T1 is set aside for H1, and the list is empty
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for T1 and Ben, loan L5
    • Then: the list has H1: T1, Ben, L5.
  • Front holder collects before the set-aside is recorded (INV-HTC-1)
    • Given: H1 is at the front of T1's queue, T1 has just been returned, and no Hold Fulfilled has been recorded
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for T1 and Ben, loan L6
    • Then: the list has H1: T1, Ben, L6.
  • Checkout with no hold (INV-HTC-1)
    • Given: Ana has no hold on the hammer (T5)
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for T5 and Ana
    • Then: the list is unchanged.
  • Someone else's checkout (INV-HTC-1)
    • Given: H1 is live on T1 and Cara, who has no hold on it, is allowed to take it (no set-aside and Ben not at the front: INV-CHK-3a does not apply)
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for T1 and Cara
    • Then: the list is unchanged.
  • Hold collected (INV-HTC-2)
    • Given: the list has H1
    • When: Hold Collected is recorded for H1
    • Then: the list is empty.
  • Cancelled before collection (INV-HTC-3)
    • Given: the list has H1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: the list is empty.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-HTC-4)
    • Given: the list has H1 once
    • When: the same Tool Checked Out is applied again
    • Then: the list still has H1 once.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-HTC-4).
  • Events for a hold no longer listed: once a row has left, a later Hold Collected or Hold Cancelled for it changes nothing.
  • The collector reads a row twice before Hold Collected lands: the list may return the same hold on two reads in a row. Collecting a hold once is Collect Hold's rule, enforced when it runs; the list need not prevent the second read.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: internal; no caller outside the Hold Collector reads it.
  • PII & compliance: ids only.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Collected (Collect Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold, and the Hold Cancelled recorded by Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost and Close Account): holdId.
    • These keys match slices/place-hold.md, slices/check-out-tool.md and slices/cancel-hold.md.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The Hold Collector reads it and issues Collect Hold.

Open Questions

None.

Slice: Collect Hold

Step 6 of 29 in Hold a tool for pickup · after Holds To Collect · before My Holds — hold collected · Automation

Intent

When a holder checks out the tool they hold, record that their hold was collected, so the hold ends as a Holds fact and the views about holds hear it from their own context. Checking out records only Tool Checked Out; Hold Collected is recorded separately, by this slice. The system does this itself; no person collects a hold.

What follows a collection is decided by the slices that read Hold Collected: the hold leaves My Holds, Holds To Fulfill's queue, Pickup Notices To Send and Pickups To Expire, and a failed pickup email for it leaves Undelivered Notices.

Trigger & Actor

  • Pattern: automation. The Hold Collector, a system processor, watches the Holds To Collect list (slices/holds-to-collect.md). Only the Hold Collector issues Collect Hold; it is not exposed to neighbors or the shed manager.
  • Triggering condition: a hold is on the list: its holder has an open loan on its tool.
  • When it acts: the list changes only when a checkout lands, so the collector acts whenever the list changes, on each item that appears.
  • What it does: it issues Collect Hold for the item's hold and loan. If the command is refused or is a repeat, nothing is recorded and the processor moves on.

Command / Input

Command: Collect Hold

HoldId and LoanId are UUIDs.

FieldTypeRequiredRules / Validation
holdIdHoldIdyesThe hold collected. Must be a hold that has been placed (INV-COL-5) and is still live (INV-COL-2).
loanIdLoanIdyesThe loan that collected it, from the list item: the holder's open loan on the hold's tool (INV-COL-3).

Trigger

Triggered by: processor Hold Collector, also in this slice, reading Holds To Collect.

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Hold Collected → context Holds Read by: Holds To Collect (the hold leaves the list), My Holds (the hold drops off), Holds To Fulfill (the hold leaves the queue), Pickup Notices To Send and Pickups To Expire (the set-aside ends), Undelivered Notices (a pickup-notice entry drops off).

FieldTypeImmutable Fact?Source / Notes
holdIdHoldIdyesFrom the command.
toolIdToolIdyesSet by the system: the tool on the hold's Hold Placed.
neighborIdNeighborIdyesSet by the system: the holder on the hold's Hold Placed.
loanIdLoanIdyesFrom the command: the loan that collected the hold.
collectedAtInstantyesSet by the system: the UTC moment the event is recorded.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Hold Collected takes the hold off Holds To Collect, My Holds, Holds To Fulfill, Pickup Notices To Send, Pickups To Expire and Undelivered Notices, each specified in its own doc and eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-COL-1: Only the Hold Collector collects holds, and only from Holds To Collect.
  • INV-COL-2: A hold is collected only while it is live: placed, and not cancelled, expired or already collected.
    • A hold cancelled in the moment between the checkout and the collector acting is refused hold-ended, and stays ended.
  • INV-COL-3: The loan named must be the holder's open loan on the hold's tool.
    • The collector takes it from the list item; a different loan is a faulty caller.
  • INV-COL-4: Collecting a hold already collected succeeds and records nothing.
  • INV-COL-5: The hold must exist.
  • INV-COL-6: Collect Hold records only Hold Collected.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ben's hold H1 is live on the cordless drill (T1), and Tool Checked Out was recorded for T1 and Ben as loan L5.

  • Happy path (INV-COL-1, INV-COL-3, INV-COL-6)
    • Given: H1 is on Holds To Collect with loan L5
    • When: the Hold Collector issues Collect Hold for H1 and L5
    • Then: Hold Collected is recorded for H1: tool T1, holder Ben, loan L5, and the moment. Nothing else is recorded.
  • Front hold collected before the set-aside (INV-COL-2)
    • Given: H1 was never fulfilled; Ben took T1 from the front of the queue
    • When: the Hold Collector issues Collect Hold for H1 and L5
    • Then: Hold Collected is recorded for H1.
  • Collected twice (INV-COL-4)
    • Given: Hold Collected has been recorded for H1
    • When: the Hold Collector issues Collect Hold for H1 and L5 again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Cancelled before the collector acts (INV-COL-2)
    • Given: Hold Cancelled was recorded for H1 after the checkout
    • When: the Hold Collector issues Collect Hold for H1 and L5
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded.
  • Wrong loan (INV-COL-3)
    • Given: H1 is on the list with loan L5
    • When: Collect Hold arrives for H1 and L9
    • Then: refused with loan-mismatch. No event is recorded.
  • Unknown hold (INV-COL-5)
    • Given: no hold has ID H9
    • When: Collect Hold arrives for H9
    • Then: refused with hold-not-found. No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

A refusal records nothing. No person sees these reasons; they are logged with the hold ID. The name is the contract; the sentence is the log text.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. hold-not-found (INV-COL-5).
  2. If Hold Collected is already recorded for the hold, the command succeeds and records nothing (INV-COL-4).
  3. hold-ended (INV-COL-2).
  4. loan-mismatch (INV-COL-3).
ReasonSentenceRule
hold-not-foundThere is no such hold.INV-COL-5
hold-endedThis hold has already ended.INV-COL-2
loan-mismatchThis loan did not collect this hold.INV-COL-3

hold-not-found and hold-ended mean the same conditions as in Cancel Hold. A missing or malformed hold ID or loan ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: a collection is identified by its hold. A repeat after Hold Collected succeeds and records nothing. The collector may read the same item twice before Hold Collected lands; the second attempt is the repeat above.

Requests at the same moment: Collect Hold is decided against the hold's events as already recorded, one at a time per hold, so at most one Hold Collected is recorded for a hold.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: internal; only the Hold Collector issues it (INV-COL-1).
  • PII & compliance: ids and a time only.
  • Performance / SLA: a hold is collected shortly after its checkout lands (seconds, not minutes); until then the hold views still show it, as the doc of each says.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold and the slices that repeat it), Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Collected (this slice): holdId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId.
    • These keys match slices/place-hold.md, slices/cancel-hold.md and slices/check-out-tool.md.
  • Read model this slice's processor reads: Holds To Collect (slices/holds-to-collect.md).
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Holds To Collect, My Holds, Holds To Fulfill, Pickup Notices To Send, Pickups To Expire and Undelivered Notices.

Open Questions

None.

Slice: My Holds

Step 2 of 29 in Hold a tool for pickup · after Place Hold · before Tool Catalog — hold placed · State View

Intent

Shows a neighbor the holds they have, on the My Holds screen: where they stand in each tool's queue, and when a tool has been set aside for them, the date to collect it by and whether the pickup email reached them. It is the only screen that tells a neighbor a tool is waiting for them, and the screen they cancel holds from.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: a neighbor, opening their own My Holds screen.
  • Whose holds it shows: the holds of the neighbor asking. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the neighbor's ID, resolving a person to their newest account, or to their closed one only when they have no newer.
  • Actions offered: nothing on this screen records anything by itself. Its one action issues a command owned by another slice:
    • Cancel (Cancel Hold slice) — offered on every listed hold (INV-MYHD-16).
    • A neighbor collects a set-aside tool with an ordinary checkout from the Tool Catalog, not from here.

Read Model / View

  • View: My Holds built from events: "Hold Placed", "Hold Collected", "Hold Cancelled", "Hold Fulfilled", "Pickup Notice Sent", "Pickup Notice Failed", "Hold Expired"
  • Consumed by: the My Holds screen (Neighbor)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events: a change shows shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Whether a set-aside's pickup window has ended is worked out when the view is read, from collectByDate and today's date in the shed's local time zone, so it is always current. No action on this screen depends on the view being instant, because Cancel Hold and Check Out Tool each check their own rules when they run.

One row per hold that hasn't ended. HoldId, ToolId, LoanId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be absent.

FieldTypeSource / Notes
holdIdHoldIdHold Placed.holdId.
neighborIdNeighborIdHold Placed.neighborId: the holder.
toolIdToolIdHold Placed.toolId.
toolNameTextHold Placed.toolName (INV-MYHD-14).
placedAtInstantHold Placed.placedAt. For display only; it doesn't decide the queue.
statusTextOne of waiting, ready-for-pickup, pickup-window-ended. Derived: see the status rules below.
positionIntDerived: while status is waiting, 1 plus the number of this tool's holds that are waiting, were placed before this one, and haven't ended (INV-MYHD-2). Optional: absent once the hold is fulfilled.
collectByDateDateDerived: Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate for this hold, read as recorded, never worked out here (INV-MYHD-3). Optional: absent while waiting.
pickupNoticeTextOne of none, sent, undelivered. Derived: sent once Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for this hold, undelivered once Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for it, none before either (INV-MYHD-13).
canCancelBoolDerived: yes on every listed hold (INV-MYHD-16).

Status rules. A hold's status is a test of its current facts, taken in this order. The first that holds wins:

  1. pickup-window-ended — Hold Fulfilled has been recorded for the hold, and today's date in the shed's local time zone is after its collectByDate (INV-MYHD-17).
  2. ready-for-pickup — otherwise, Hold Fulfilled has been recorded for the hold.
  3. waiting — otherwise.

When a hold leaves the view. A hold is listed from Hold Placed until it ends. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, or when the holder checks the tool out. In events:

  • Hold Cancelled or Hold Expired for the hold;
  • Hold Collected for the hold (the holder checked the tool out).

Retiring the tool, recording it lost and closing the holder's account each end holds by recording Hold Cancelled for them (Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost, Close Account). This view hears only the Holds events.

Queue order. A tool's queue is the order in which Hold Placed was recorded for it. To work out positions, the view keeps, for each tool, every hold on it that hasn't ended, with its holder and whether it has been fulfilled. This is bookkeeping, not part of the row, and other neighbors' holds are never returned.

Queries

  • List my holds. Takes the asking neighbor's neighborId. Returns every hold of that neighbor that hasn't ended, each with every field above, and nothing about anyone else's holds (INV-MYHD-1). There is no paging. A neighbor with no holds gets an empty list. Holds are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when the hold was placed, in the order Hold Placed was recorded (INV-MYHD-18).

Invariants / Business Rules

A neighbor has at most one hold on any one tool, because Place Hold refuses a second (INV-HOLD-7, Place Hold). A suspended neighbor can't place a new hold (INV-HOLD-9) or collect a set-aside tool (INV-CHK-7), but may still cancel. An expired hold sends no message, doesn't count against the neighbor, and the neighbor may place a new hold on the tool at the back of the queue (Expire Hold). A suspended neighbor keeps their holds and their place in each queue. A front holder who can't collect, because they are suspended or have an overdue loan, still has the tool set aside for them, and the pickup window runs regardless (Fulfill Hold, INV-FUL-8). These rules are owned by those slices; this view just reflects the events they record, and it doesn't hear suspension or loans at all (INV-MYHD-11).

  • INV-MYHD-1: A neighbor's My Holds shows only their own holds.
    • The query returns only holds whose holder is the neighbor ID it is given. It never shows who else holds a tool, only the neighbor's own position. No neighbor-facing screen ever shows who has a tool or who holds one; only the shed manager sees borrowers, on Tool Inventory.
  • INV-MYHD-2: Holds on a tool queue in the order they were placed. Each waiting hold shows the neighbor's position in that tool's queue.
    • Position 1 is the next hold to be fulfilled. A hold moves up as holds ahead of it are fulfilled or end.
    • A hold that has been fulfilled is no longer in the waiting queue, so the first waiting hold behind a set-aside is at position 1.
  • INV-MYHD-3: Once a neighbor's hold is fulfilled, My Holds shows the tool as ready for pickup, with the date to collect it by.
    • The collect-by date is the one Hold Fulfilled carries: the date the tool was set aside plus 3 days. My Holds shows it as recorded and never works it out itself.
    • My Holds is the only screen that tells a neighbor a tool is set aside for them. The Tool Catalog is the same for every neighbor.
  • INV-MYHD-4: A hold that is ready for pickup stays on My Holds until the holder collects it, cancels it, or Hold Expired is recorded for it. Then it drops off.
    • The tool then passes to the next hold, which shows as ready for pickup on that neighbor's My Holds once Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • INV-MYHD-5: When a holder checks out the tool they hold, their hold ends and drops off My Holds, whether or not it had been fulfilled.
    • The loan then appears on My Loans.
  • INV-MYHD-6: A cancelled hold drops off My Holds, whether it was waiting or ready for pickup.
    • Cancelling a hold that is ready for pickup passes the tool to the next hold, the same as expiry.
  • INV-MYHD-7: Retiring a tool, or recording it lost, ends every hold on it, and those holds drop off My Holds.
    • Retire Tool and Record Tool Lost record Hold Cancelled for each hold; this view hears those. The holders are not told.
  • INV-MYHD-8: Closing an account ends all of that neighbor's holds. Their holds drop off My Holds, and holds behind them move up.
    • Close Account records Hold Cancelled for each of the neighbor's holds; this view hears those.
    • A tool that was ready for pickup for them passes to the next hold, the same as expiry.
  • INV-MYHD-13: Once a tool is set aside for a neighbor, My Holds shows whether the pickup email was sent or couldn't be delivered.
    • If the email can't be delivered, the tool stays ready for pickup, with the same collect-by date.
  • INV-MYHD-14: Each hold shows the tool's name.
    • The name comes with Hold Placed, which carries it.
  • INV-MYHD-11: Only Hold Placed, Hold Collected, Hold Cancelled, Hold Fulfilled, Pickup Notice Sent, Pickup Notice Failed and Hold Expired change My Holds.
    • A checkout records Hold Collected only when the borrower had a hold on the tool; a checkout by anyone else is not heard here at all.
  • INV-MYHD-15: Applying the same event twice leaves My Holds as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-MYHD-16: My Holds offers Cancel on every hold it lists.
    • That includes holds ready for pickup, holds whose pickup window has ended, and holds of a suspended neighbor.
  • INV-MYHD-17: Once a set-aside's collect-by date has passed, My Holds shows that the pickup window has ended, even before Hold Expired is recorded.
    • From the start of the day after the collect-by date, in the shed's local time, the set-aside is no longer theirs: the tool goes to the next neighbor in the queue, or to whoever checks it out first if nobody is waiting (INV-CHK-3b, Check Out Tool). The hold drops off when Hold Expired is recorded.
  • INV-MYHD-18: Holds are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when they were placed.
  • INV-MYHD-19: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.
  • INV-MYHD-20: My Holds is answered only for the signed-in neighbor: a request for any other neighbor ID is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Hold placed (INV-MYHD-2, INV-MYHD-14, INV-MYHD-16)
    • Given: Ana has T1, the "Cordless drill", on loan, and nobody has a hold on it
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's hold H1 on T1, carrying the name "Cordless drill"
    • Then: Ben's My Holds lists H1: "Cordless drill", waiting, position 1, pickup notice none, with Cancel offered.
  • A second hold placed (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Cara's hold H2 on T1
    • Then: Cara's My Holds lists H2, waiting, position 2. Ben's is unchanged.
  • Holds placed in the same instant (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Cara's H2 and then Dan's H3 on T1, with the same placedAt
    • Then: H2 is at position 2 and H3 at position 3: the order recorded decides, not placedAt.
  • Hold cancelled (INV-MYHD-6, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Hold fulfilled (INV-MYHD-3, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1, and T1 has been returned
    • When: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1, with the collect-by date 17 October
    • Then: Ben's My Holds shows H1 ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, with no position. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Pickup email sent (INV-MYHD-13)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, pickup notice none
    • When: Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 shows pickup notice sent.
  • Pickup email couldn't be delivered (INV-MYHD-13)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, pickup notice sent
    • When: Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 shows pickup notice undelivered, still ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October.
  • Collect-by date is the last day (INV-MYHD-17)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October
    • When: his holds are listed at 23:59 on 17 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 is ready-for-pickup.
  • Pickup window ended, not yet expired (INV-MYHD-17, INV-MYHD-16)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded
    • When: his holds are listed at 00:00 on 18 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 shows pickup-window-ended, with Cancel still offered.
  • Hold expired (INV-MYHD-4)
    • Given: Ben's H1 shows pickup-window-ended, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 stays waiting at position 1 until Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • Suspended holder (INV-MYHD-3, INV-MYHD-11)
    • Given: Ben is suspended, and his H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: T1 is returned and Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1, collect by 17 October
    • Then: Ben's My Holds shows H1 ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October.
  • Holder collects the tool (INV-MYHD-5)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Collected is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's is unchanged.
  • Front holder collects before the set-aside is recorded (INV-MYHD-5, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1, and T1 has just been returned
    • When: Hold Collected is recorded for H1, before any Hold Fulfilled
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Ready-for-pickup hold cancelled (INV-MYHD-6)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 stays waiting until Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • Tool retired (INV-MYHD-7)
    • Given: Ben's H1 and Cara's H2 are on T1
    • When: Retire Tool records Hold Cancelled for H1 and for H2, with Tool Retired for T1
    • Then: H1 and H2 drop off both neighbors' My Holds.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-MYHD-7)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan as loan L1, and Ben's H1 and Cara's H2 are on T1
    • When: Record Tool Lost records Hold Cancelled for H1 and for H2, with Tool Lost for L1
    • Then: H1 and H2 drop off both neighbors' My Holds.
  • Holder closes their account (INV-MYHD-8)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1
    • When: Close Account records Hold Cancelled for H1, with Neighbor Account Closed for Ben
    • Then: H1 drops off. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Hold again after expiry (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 expired, and T1 is now set aside for Cara's H2
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's new hold H4 on T1
    • Then: Ben's My Holds lists H4, waiting, position 1, behind Cara's set-aside.
  • Only their own holds (INV-MYHD-1)
    • Given: Ben has H1 and Cara has H2, both on T1
    • When: Ben's holds are listed
    • Then: only H1 is returned, with its position. Nothing about H2 or Cara is returned.
  • List order (INV-MYHD-18)
    • Given: Ben placed H5 on the ladder, then H1 on the cordless drill
    • When: his holds are listed
    • Then: H1 (cordless drill) comes first, then H5 (ladder).
  • Same event applied twice (INV-MYHD-15)
    • Given: Ben's My Holds lists H1 at position 1
    • When: the same Hold Placed for H1 is applied again
    • Then: Ben's My Holds still lists H1 once, at position 1, and no later hold's position changes.
  • Not signed in (INV-MYHD-19)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: My Holds is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.
  • Asked by the wrong person (INV-MYHD-20)
    • Given: Ben (N2) is signed in
    • When: the holds of N1, Ana, are asked for
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only see your own holds." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

Reading this view is guarded like a command. A refused read returns nothing and one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown on the screen. The checks run in this order:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-MYHD-19).
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-MYHD-20).
ReasonSentenceRule
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-MYHD-19
requester-mismatchYou can only see your own holds.INV-MYHD-20
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-MYHD-15). An event applied a second time leaves the view as it was after the first.
  • Events for a hold that has ended: once a hold has ended it is gone from this view. A later event for it (a replay, or a Pickup Notice Failed that arrives after the set-aside ended) changes nothing.
  • Stale actions: Cancel offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, just as the hold expires or the tool is collected). Cancel Hold checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may list only their own holds (INV-MYHD-1). The query is always asked for the signed-in neighbor's own ID, which sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies; a request for any other neighbor ID is refused requester-mismatch (INV-MYHD-20), and one with no sign-in not-signed-in (INV-MYHD-19).
  • PII & compliance: shows a neighbor their own holds only, and never who else holds or has a tool. The other holders and borrowers it keeps for working out positions are never returned.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId, placedAt.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, collectByDate.
    • Pickup Notice Sent (Send Pickup Notice): holdId.
    • Pickup Notice Failed (Record Pickup Notice Failure): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Collected (Collect Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Cancelled is also recorded by Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost and Close Account, one per hold they end; this view can't tell those from a holder's own cancellation and needn't.
    • Hold Placed and Hold Collected match slices/place-hold.md and slices/check-out-tool.md. The others are specified in slices not yet written in depth; these keys are this view's assumptions, and each is checked when that slice is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Cancel Hold.

Open Questions

None.

Slice: Cancel Hold

Step 9 of 29 in Hold a tool for pickup · after Undelivered Notices — hold collected · before My Holds — hold cancelled · State Change

Intent

Let a neighbor give up a hold they no longer want, from My Holds, so the tool goes to the next neighbor in the queue instead of waiting on them. A hold can be cancelled while it is waiting or while the tool is set aside for the holder, and a suspended neighbor can cancel too.

What follows a cancellation is decided by the views and slices that read Hold Cancelled:

  • Every hold behind the cancelled one on that tool moves up one place (My Holds, Holds To Fulfill).
  • Cancelling a hold that is ready for pickup ends the set-aside. The tool passes to the next hold, or becomes available if none is waiting (Holds To Fulfill, Tool Catalog), the same as when a set-aside expires.
  • A cancelled hold gives up its place for good. The neighbor may place a new hold on the same tool, which joins the back of the queue (Place Hold, INV-HOLD-7: only a live hold counts).

Trigger & Actor

The holder, from the My Holds screen, on one of their own holds that hasn't ended. The shed manager doesn't cancel holds. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the acting neighbor's ID.

Command / Input

Command: Cancel Hold

A HoldId or NeighborId is a UUID.

FieldTypeRequiredRules / Validation
holdIdHoldIdyesThe hold to cancel. Must be a hold that has been placed (INV-CNH-7).
neighborIdNeighborIdyesThe neighbor cancelling, who must be the one making the request (requester-mismatch) and the hold's holder (not-your-hold) (INV-CNH-1).

Trigger

Triggered by: screen My Holds @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Hold Cancelled → context Holds Read by: My Holds and Tool Catalog (their continuations right after this slice), My Loans (whether a hold is still waiting on a borrowed tool), Holds To Fulfill and Pickups To Expire (the hold's queue and set-aside), Pickup Notices To Send (no pickup email for a cancelled set-aside), and Undelivered Notices (a failed pickup email's entry drops off).

FieldTypeImmutable Fact?Source / Notes
holdIdHoldIdyesFrom the command. The tool and holder are those on the hold's Hold Placed.
cancelledAtInstantyesThe UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.

The event doesn't say whether the hold was waiting or set aside. Readers already know from Hold Placed and Hold Fulfilled.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Hold Cancelled ends the hold in My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans and the hold to-do lists, each specified in its own doc. All are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-CNH-1: A neighbor can cancel only their own hold, and does it themselves.
    • The command names the acting neighbor in neighborId. The request must come from that neighbor (requester-mismatch), and the hold must be theirs (not-your-hold). The shed manager does not cancel holds. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the acting neighbor's ID.
    • A caller with no sign-in is refused with not-signed-in, before anything else is checked.
  • INV-CNH-2: A hold can be cancelled while it is waiting or while the tool is set aside for the holder.
    • A suspended neighbor may cancel their own hold. Cancelling only gives up their own claim.
    • A set-aside whose collect-by date has passed, but whose Hold Expired hasn't been recorded yet, hasn't ended, so it can still be cancelled. Either way the tool passes on.
  • INV-CNH-3: A hold that has ended in any way other than being cancelled can't be cancelled.
    • A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, the holder checks the tool out, the tool is retired or recorded lost, or the holder closes their account.
    • A hold the holder has already cancelled is covered by INV-CNH-8.
  • INV-CNH-7: The hold must exist.
  • INV-CNH-8: Cancelling a hold that is already cancelled succeeds and records nothing new.
    • So a double submit, or a retry after a lost response, never fails and never records a second Hold Cancelled.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ben and Cara are active neighbors, and Ben's hold H1 on the cordless drill was placed before Cara's hold H2.

  • Cancel a waiting hold (INV-CNH-2)
    • Given: the drill is checked out by Ana, and H1 and H2 are waiting
    • When: Ben cancels H1 from My Holds
    • Then: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1.
  • Cancel a hold that is ready for pickup (INV-CNH-2)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben under H1, with a collect-by date of 17 October, and H2 is waiting
    • When: Ben cancels H1 on 15 October
    • Then: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1.
  • Cancel a lapsed set-aside before its expiry is recorded (INV-CNH-2)
    • Given: the drill was set aside for Ben under H1, to collect by 17 October. It is 18 October and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded for H1.
    • When: Ben cancels H1
    • Then: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1, and no Hold Expired follows for it.
  • Suspended neighbor cancels a hold (INV-CNH-2)
    • Given: Ben is suspended, and H1 is waiting
    • When: Ben cancels H1
    • Then: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-CNH-8)
    • Given: Hold Cancelled has been recorded for H1
    • When: the same request to cancel H1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • A request that doesn't come from the neighbor it names (INV-CNH-1)
    • Given: H1 is Ben's waiting hold
    • When: a request to cancel H1, naming Ben, comes from someone other than Ben
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only cancel holds for yourself." No event is recorded.
  • Someone else's hold (INV-CNH-1)
    • Given: H1 is Ben's waiting hold
    • When: Cara, naming herself, tries to cancel H1
    • Then: refused with not-your-hold: "You can only cancel your own holds." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown hold (INV-CNH-7)
    • Given: no hold H9 has been placed
    • When: a request to cancel H9 arrives
    • Then: refused with hold-not-found: "There is no such hold." No event is recorded.
  • Hold already expired (INV-CNH-3)
    • Given: Hold Expired has been recorded for H1
    • When: Ben tries to cancel H1
    • Then: refused with hold-ended: "This hold has already ended." No event is recorded.
  • Hold ended by the holder's checkout (INV-CNH-3)
    • Given: Ben checked out the drill as H1's holder, which ended H1
    • When: Ben tries to cancel H1
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded.
  • Hold ended by retirement (INV-CNH-3)
    • Given: the drill was retired while H1 was waiting
    • When: Ben tries to cancel H1
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded.
  • Hold ended because the tool was recorded lost (INV-CNH-3)
    • Given: Tool Lost was recorded for Ana's loan of the drill while H1 was waiting
    • When: Ben tries to cancel H1
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded.
  • Hold ended by closing the account (INV-CNH-3)
    • Given: Ben closed his account while H1 was waiting
    • When: a request to cancel H1 for Ben arrives
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded.
  • No sign-in (INV-CNH-1)
    • Given: a caller with no sign-in
    • When: they ask to cancel H1
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the neighbor on the My Holds screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in, then requester-mismatch (INV-CNH-1).
  2. hold-not-found (INV-CNH-7).
  3. not-your-hold (INV-CNH-1).
  4. If Hold Cancelled is already recorded for the hold, the request succeeds and records nothing (INV-CNH-8).
  5. hold-ended (INV-CNH-3).
ReasonSentenceRule
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-CNH-1
requester-mismatchYou can only cancel holds for yourself.INV-CNH-1
hold-not-foundThere is no such hold.INV-CNH-7
not-your-holdYou can only cancel your own holds.INV-CNH-1
hold-endedThis hold has already ended.INV-CNH-3

hold-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name. hold-not-found is worded the same wherever a hold is looked up.

Idempotency: cancelling is safe to repeat (INV-CNH-8). A repeat records nothing, whatever has happened since.

Requests at the same moment: each cancellation is decided against the hold's events as already recorded, one at a time per hold. If the holder cancels just as the hold ends another way (the fulfiller sets the tool aside, the expirer expires it, or the tool is retired), whichever is recorded first stands. A cancel decided after an expiry, retirement or closure is refused with hold-ended. A cancel decided after Hold Fulfilled cancels the set-aside.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice. Cancelling sends no email.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the holder may cancel their own hold (INV-CNH-1). Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the acting neighbor's ID.
  • PII & compliance: Hold Cancelled holds only the hold's ID and a time. No name or email.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time rule above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Cancelled (this slice): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): toolId, neighborId (the holder's own checkout ends their hold on that tool).
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): toolId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These keys match slices/place-hold.md, check-out-tool.md and tool-catalog.md. Hold Cancelled adds cancelledAt; readers that need only {holdId} are unaffected.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans, Holds To Fulfill, Pickups To Expire, Pickup Notices To Send and Undelivered Notices. Place Hold accepts a new hold from the same neighbor on the same tool once this one is cancelled.

Open Questions

  • Dependencies: Tool Lost is matched by its own toolId, not through Tool Checked Out.loanId (conformance 2026-11-01, finding 5) — v2: Dependencies reworded; behaviour unchanged (2026-11-01)
