Slice: My Holds

Step 2 of 29 in Hold a tool for pickup · after Place Hold · before Tool Catalog — hold placed · State View

Intent

Shows a neighbor the holds they have, on the My Holds screen: where they stand in each tool's queue, and when a tool has been set aside for them, the date to collect it by and whether the pickup email reached them. It is the only screen that tells a neighbor a tool is waiting for them, and the screen they cancel holds from.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: a neighbor, opening their own My Holds screen.
  • Whose holds it shows: the holds of the neighbor asking. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the neighbor's ID, resolving a person to their newest account, or to their closed one only when they have no newer.
  • Actions offered: nothing on this screen records anything by itself. Its one action issues a command owned by another slice:
    • Cancel (Cancel Hold slice) — offered on every listed hold (INV-MYHD-16).
    • A neighbor collects a set-aside tool with an ordinary checkout from the Tool Catalog, not from here.

Read Model / View

  • View: My Holds built from events: "Hold Placed", "Hold Collected", "Hold Cancelled", "Hold Fulfilled", "Pickup Notice Sent", "Pickup Notice Failed", "Hold Expired"
  • Consumed by: the My Holds screen (Neighbor)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events: a change shows shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Whether a set-aside's pickup window has ended is worked out when the view is read, from collectByDate and today's date in the shed's local time zone, so it is always current. No action on this screen depends on the view being instant, because Cancel Hold and Check Out Tool each check their own rules when they run.

One row per hold that hasn't ended. HoldId, ToolId, LoanId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be absent.

FieldTypeSource / Notes
holdIdHoldIdHold Placed.holdId.
neighborIdNeighborIdHold Placed.neighborId: the holder.
toolIdToolIdHold Placed.toolId.
toolNameTextHold Placed.toolName (INV-MYHD-14).
placedAtInstantHold Placed.placedAt. For display only; it doesn't decide the queue.
statusTextOne of waiting, ready-for-pickup, pickup-window-ended. Derived: see the status rules below.
positionIntDerived: while status is waiting, 1 plus the number of this tool's holds that are waiting, were placed before this one, and haven't ended (INV-MYHD-2). Optional: absent once the hold is fulfilled.
collectByDateDateDerived: Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate for this hold, read as recorded, never worked out here (INV-MYHD-3). Optional: absent while waiting.
pickupNoticeTextOne of none, sent, undelivered. Derived: sent once Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for this hold, undelivered once Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for it, none before either (INV-MYHD-13).
canCancelBoolDerived: yes on every listed hold (INV-MYHD-16).

Status rules. A hold's status is a test of its current facts, taken in this order. The first that holds wins:

  1. pickup-window-ended — Hold Fulfilled has been recorded for the hold, and today's date in the shed's local time zone is after its collectByDate (INV-MYHD-17).
  2. ready-for-pickup — otherwise, Hold Fulfilled has been recorded for the hold.
  3. waiting — otherwise.

When a hold leaves the view. A hold is listed from Hold Placed until it ends. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, or when the holder checks the tool out. In events:

  • Hold Cancelled or Hold Expired for the hold;
  • Hold Collected for the hold (the holder checked the tool out).

Retiring the tool, recording it lost and closing the holder's account each end holds by recording Hold Cancelled for them (Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost, Close Account). This view hears only the Holds events.

Queue order. A tool's queue is the order in which Hold Placed was recorded for it. To work out positions, the view keeps, for each tool, every hold on it that hasn't ended, with its holder and whether it has been fulfilled. This is bookkeeping, not part of the row, and other neighbors' holds are never returned.

Queries

  • List my holds. Takes the asking neighbor's neighborId. Returns every hold of that neighbor that hasn't ended, each with every field above, and nothing about anyone else's holds (INV-MYHD-1). There is no paging. A neighbor with no holds gets an empty list. Holds are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when the hold was placed, in the order Hold Placed was recorded (INV-MYHD-18).

Invariants / Business Rules

A neighbor has at most one hold on any one tool, because Place Hold refuses a second (INV-HOLD-7, Place Hold). A suspended neighbor can't place a new hold (INV-HOLD-9) or collect a set-aside tool (INV-CHK-7), but may still cancel. An expired hold sends no message, doesn't count against the neighbor, and the neighbor may place a new hold on the tool at the back of the queue (Expire Hold). A suspended neighbor keeps their holds and their place in each queue. A front holder who can't collect, because they are suspended or have an overdue loan, still has the tool set aside for them, and the pickup window runs regardless (Fulfill Hold, INV-FUL-8). These rules are owned by those slices; this view just reflects the events they record, and it doesn't hear suspension or loans at all (INV-MYHD-11).

  • INV-MYHD-1: A neighbor's My Holds shows only their own holds.
    • The query returns only holds whose holder is the neighbor ID it is given. It never shows who else holds a tool, only the neighbor's own position. No neighbor-facing screen ever shows who has a tool or who holds one; only the shed manager sees borrowers, on Tool Inventory.
  • INV-MYHD-2: Holds on a tool queue in the order they were placed. Each waiting hold shows the neighbor's position in that tool's queue.
    • Position 1 is the next hold to be fulfilled. A hold moves up as holds ahead of it are fulfilled or end.
    • A hold that has been fulfilled is no longer in the waiting queue, so the first waiting hold behind a set-aside is at position 1.
  • INV-MYHD-3: Once a neighbor's hold is fulfilled, My Holds shows the tool as ready for pickup, with the date to collect it by.
    • The collect-by date is the one Hold Fulfilled carries: the date the tool was set aside plus 3 days. My Holds shows it as recorded and never works it out itself.
    • My Holds is the only screen that tells a neighbor a tool is set aside for them. The Tool Catalog is the same for every neighbor.
  • INV-MYHD-4: A hold that is ready for pickup stays on My Holds until the holder collects it, cancels it, or Hold Expired is recorded for it. Then it drops off.
    • The tool then passes to the next hold, which shows as ready for pickup on that neighbor's My Holds once Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • INV-MYHD-5: When a holder checks out the tool they hold, their hold ends and drops off My Holds, whether or not it had been fulfilled.
    • The loan then appears on My Loans.
  • INV-MYHD-6: A cancelled hold drops off My Holds, whether it was waiting or ready for pickup.
    • Cancelling a hold that is ready for pickup passes the tool to the next hold, the same as expiry.
  • INV-MYHD-7: Retiring a tool, or recording it lost, ends every hold on it, and those holds drop off My Holds.
    • Retire Tool and Record Tool Lost record Hold Cancelled for each hold; this view hears those. The holders are not told.
  • INV-MYHD-8: Closing an account ends all of that neighbor's holds. Their holds drop off My Holds, and holds behind them move up.
    • Close Account records Hold Cancelled for each of the neighbor's holds; this view hears those.
    • A tool that was ready for pickup for them passes to the next hold, the same as expiry.
  • INV-MYHD-13: Once a tool is set aside for a neighbor, My Holds shows whether the pickup email was sent or couldn't be delivered.
    • If the email can't be delivered, the tool stays ready for pickup, with the same collect-by date.
  • INV-MYHD-14: Each hold shows the tool's name.
    • The name comes with Hold Placed, which carries it.
  • INV-MYHD-11: Only Hold Placed, Hold Collected, Hold Cancelled, Hold Fulfilled, Pickup Notice Sent, Pickup Notice Failed and Hold Expired change My Holds.
    • A checkout records Hold Collected only when the borrower had a hold on the tool; a checkout by anyone else is not heard here at all.
  • INV-MYHD-15: Applying the same event twice leaves My Holds as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-MYHD-16: My Holds offers Cancel on every hold it lists.
    • That includes holds ready for pickup, holds whose pickup window has ended, and holds of a suspended neighbor.
  • INV-MYHD-17: Once a set-aside's collect-by date has passed, My Holds shows that the pickup window has ended, even before Hold Expired is recorded.
    • From the start of the day after the collect-by date, in the shed's local time, the set-aside is no longer theirs: the tool goes to the next neighbor in the queue, or to whoever checks it out first if nobody is waiting (INV-CHK-3b, Check Out Tool). The hold drops off when Hold Expired is recorded.
  • INV-MYHD-18: Holds are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when they were placed.
  • INV-MYHD-19: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.
  • INV-MYHD-20: My Holds is answered only for the signed-in neighbor: a request for any other neighbor ID is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Hold placed (INV-MYHD-2, INV-MYHD-14, INV-MYHD-16)
    • Given: Ana has T1, the "Cordless drill", on loan, and nobody has a hold on it
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's hold H1 on T1, carrying the name "Cordless drill"
    • Then: Ben's My Holds lists H1: "Cordless drill", waiting, position 1, pickup notice none, with Cancel offered.
  • A second hold placed (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Cara's hold H2 on T1
    • Then: Cara's My Holds lists H2, waiting, position 2. Ben's is unchanged.
  • Holds placed in the same instant (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Cara's H2 and then Dan's H3 on T1, with the same placedAt
    • Then: H2 is at position 2 and H3 at position 3: the order recorded decides, not placedAt.
  • Hold cancelled (INV-MYHD-6, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Hold fulfilled (INV-MYHD-3, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1, and T1 has been returned
    • When: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1, with the collect-by date 17 October
    • Then: Ben's My Holds shows H1 ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, with no position. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Pickup email sent (INV-MYHD-13)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, pickup notice none
    • When: Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 shows pickup notice sent.
  • Pickup email couldn't be delivered (INV-MYHD-13)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, pickup notice sent
    • When: Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 shows pickup notice undelivered, still ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October.
  • Collect-by date is the last day (INV-MYHD-17)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October
    • When: his holds are listed at 23:59 on 17 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 is ready-for-pickup.
  • Pickup window ended, not yet expired (INV-MYHD-17, INV-MYHD-16)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded
    • When: his holds are listed at 00:00 on 18 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 shows pickup-window-ended, with Cancel still offered.
  • Hold expired (INV-MYHD-4)
    • Given: Ben's H1 shows pickup-window-ended, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 stays waiting at position 1 until Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • Suspended holder (INV-MYHD-3, INV-MYHD-11)
    • Given: Ben is suspended, and his H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: T1 is returned and Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1, collect by 17 October
    • Then: Ben's My Holds shows H1 ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October.
  • Holder collects the tool (INV-MYHD-5)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Collected is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's is unchanged.
  • Front holder collects before the set-aside is recorded (INV-MYHD-5, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1, and T1 has just been returned
    • When: Hold Collected is recorded for H1, before any Hold Fulfilled
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Ready-for-pickup hold cancelled (INV-MYHD-6)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 stays waiting until Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • Tool retired (INV-MYHD-7)
    • Given: Ben's H1 and Cara's H2 are on T1
    • When: Retire Tool records Hold Cancelled for H1 and for H2, with Tool Retired for T1
    • Then: H1 and H2 drop off both neighbors' My Holds.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-MYHD-7)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan as loan L1, and Ben's H1 and Cara's H2 are on T1
    • When: Record Tool Lost records Hold Cancelled for H1 and for H2, with Tool Lost for L1
    • Then: H1 and H2 drop off both neighbors' My Holds.
  • Holder closes their account (INV-MYHD-8)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1
    • When: Close Account records Hold Cancelled for H1, with Neighbor Account Closed for Ben
    • Then: H1 drops off. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Hold again after expiry (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 expired, and T1 is now set aside for Cara's H2
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's new hold H4 on T1
    • Then: Ben's My Holds lists H4, waiting, position 1, behind Cara's set-aside.
  • Only their own holds (INV-MYHD-1)
    • Given: Ben has H1 and Cara has H2, both on T1
    • When: Ben's holds are listed
    • Then: only H1 is returned, with its position. Nothing about H2 or Cara is returned.
  • List order (INV-MYHD-18)
    • Given: Ben placed H5 on the ladder, then H1 on the cordless drill
    • When: his holds are listed
    • Then: H1 (cordless drill) comes first, then H5 (ladder).
  • Same event applied twice (INV-MYHD-15)
    • Given: Ben's My Holds lists H1 at position 1
    • When: the same Hold Placed for H1 is applied again
    • Then: Ben's My Holds still lists H1 once, at position 1, and no later hold's position changes.
  • Not signed in (INV-MYHD-19)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: My Holds is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.
  • Asked by the wrong person (INV-MYHD-20)
    • Given: Ben (N2) is signed in
    • When: the holds of N1, Ana, are asked for
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only see your own holds." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

Reading this view is guarded like a command. A refused read returns nothing and one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown on the screen. The checks run in this order:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-MYHD-19).
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-MYHD-20).
ReasonSentenceRule
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-MYHD-19
requester-mismatchYou can only see your own holds.INV-MYHD-20
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-MYHD-15). An event applied a second time leaves the view as it was after the first.
  • Events for a hold that has ended: once a hold has ended it is gone from this view. A later event for it (a replay, or a Pickup Notice Failed that arrives after the set-aside ended) changes nothing.
  • Stale actions: Cancel offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, just as the hold expires or the tool is collected). Cancel Hold checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may list only their own holds (INV-MYHD-1). The query is always asked for the signed-in neighbor's own ID, which sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies; a request for any other neighbor ID is refused requester-mismatch (INV-MYHD-20), and one with no sign-in not-signed-in (INV-MYHD-19).
  • PII & compliance: shows a neighbor their own holds only, and never who else holds or has a tool. The other holders and borrowers it keeps for working out positions are never returned.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId, placedAt.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, collectByDate.
    • Pickup Notice Sent (Send Pickup Notice): holdId.
    • Pickup Notice Failed (Record Pickup Notice Failure): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Collected (Collect Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Cancelled is also recorded by Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost and Close Account, one per hold they end; this view can't tell those from a holder's own cancellation and needn't.
    • Hold Placed and Hold Collected match slices/place-hold.md and slices/check-out-tool.md. The others are specified in slices not yet written in depth; these keys are this view's assumptions, and each is checked when that slice is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Cancel Hold.

Open Questions

None.

Slice: Holds To Fulfill

Step 14 of 29 in Hold a tool for pickup · after Undelivered Notices — hold cancelled · before Fulfill Hold · State View

Intent

The hold fulfiller's to-do list: every tool that is back in the shed, not set aside for anyone, with a hold waiting, and which hold is next in line for it. The hold fulfiller works through it, so a returned tool is set aside for the neighbor at the front of its queue.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the Hold Fulfiller, a system reaction in the Fulfill Hold slice. No person reads this list, and it has no screen.
  • What the fulfiller does with it: for each tool on the list, it issues Fulfill Hold for the front hold, which records Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold slice).

Read Model / View

  • View: Holds To Fulfill built from events: "Hold Placed", "Hold Collected", "Tool Returned", "Hold Cancelled", "Tool Checked Out", "Hold Fulfilled", "Hold Expired"
  • Consumed by: the Hold Fulfiller (Fulfill Hold). Internal: no ui.
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. A tool joins or leaves the list shortly after the event that causes it is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Fulfill Hold checks its own rules when it runs, so acting on a row a moment out of date sets nothing aside wrongly.

One row per tool on the list. ToolId, HoldId and NeighborId are UUIDs.

FieldTypeSource / Notes
toolIdToolIdHold Placed.toolId.
holdIdHoldIdDerived: the front hold: the first hold on toolId, in the order Hold Placed was recorded, that is still waiting (INV-HTF-2).
neighborIdNeighborIdDerived: the front hold's holder, from its Hold Placed.

Bookkeeping. For every tool that has holds, the view keeps: whether a loan of it is open (from Tool Checked Out until Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan); whether a hold on it is set aside (from Hold Fulfilled until that hold ends); and its waiting holds, with holder, in the order Hold Placed was recorded. None of this is returned except the row.

Waiting and ending. A hold is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends. A hold ends when Hold Cancelled, Hold Expired or Hold Collected is recorded for it. Retiring the tool, recording it lost and closing the holder's account each end holds by recording Hold Cancelled for them (Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost, Close Account). This list hears only the Holds events for holds.

Queries

  • List tools to fulfill. Takes nothing. Returns every row: toolId, and the front hold's holdId and neighborId. There is no paging. The order doesn't matter to the fulfiller, which acts on each tool separately.

Invariants / Business Rules

The list has no screen; only the hold fulfiller reads it. The front holder is never passed over, even when they are suspended or have an overdue loan and can't collect: the tool is set aside for them, and if they don't collect it by the end of the collect-by date the hold expires (Fulfill Hold, INV-FUL-8; Expire Hold). This view doesn't hear suspension or loans of other tools, so it never skips anyone.

  • INV-HTF-1: A tool is on the list exactly when all of these hold, tested against its current facts: no loan of it is open, no hold on it is set aside, and at least one hold on it is waiting.
    • A loan is open from Tool Checked Out until Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan. A hold is set aside from Hold Fulfilled until it ends; a set-aside whose collect-by date has passed still counts until Hold Expired is recorded for it.
    • The test reads current facts, not the order events arrived in. So a tool on loan is never on the list, however many holds wait on it, and whatever ended its last set-aside.
  • INV-HTF-2: Each item names the hold at the front of the tool's queue: the earliest-placed hold still waiting.
    • "Earliest-placed" is the order Hold Placed was recorded for the tool, not placedAt, since two holds can share a timestamp.
  • INV-HTF-3: When one of its holds is fulfilled, the tool leaves the list: the hold is now set aside (INV-HTF-1).
  • INV-HTF-4: When a set-aside ends without the holder collecting it (the hold expires or is cancelled, including by the holder closing their account), the tool joins the list if INV-HTF-1 then holds: no loan open and another hold waiting.
    • With no hold waiting, the tool becomes available and stays off the list. If someone checked it out after the collect-by date and before Hold Expired, it stays off the list until that loan ends.
  • INV-HTF-5: When the holder at the front of the queue checks the tool out before their hold is fulfilled, the tool leaves the list: a loan is now open, and that checkout ended their hold.
    • The next hold waits for the tool's return.
  • INV-HTF-6: When a waiting hold ends, the next waiting hold becomes the front. If no hold is left waiting, the tool leaves the list (INV-HTF-1).
  • INV-HTF-7: Retiring a tool, or recording it lost, ends all its holds: Retire Tool and Record Tool Lost record Hold Cancelled for each. With no hold left waiting, the tool leaves the list, or never joins it.
    • A tool is recorded lost only while it is on loan, so it is never on the list at that moment. Its holds are cancelled, and it never comes onto the list.
    • A tool retired while on loan never joins the list when it is returned: its holds were cancelled with it.
  • INV-HTF-9: Applying the same event twice leaves the list as if it had been applied once.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Returned with a hold waiting (INV-HTF-1, INV-HTF-2)
    • Given: Ana has the cordless drill (T1) on loan L1, and Ben's hold H1 on it was placed before Cleo's hold H2
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for L1, tool T1
    • Then: T1 is on the list, with front hold H1, Ben.
  • Returned with no hold waiting (INV-HTF-1)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan L1, with no holds on it
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for L1
    • Then: T1 is not on the list.
  • Hold placed on a tool on loan (INV-HTF-1)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's hold H1 on T1
    • Then: T1 is not on the list.
  • Holds placed in the same instant (INV-HTF-2)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for H1 (Ben) and then H2 (Cleo), both with the same placedAt, and Tool Returned is then recorded for Ana's loan
    • Then: T1 is on the list with front hold H1: the order recorded decides.
  • Hold fulfilled (INV-HTF-3)
    • Given: T1 is on the list, with front hold H1 and H2 behind it
    • When: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1
    • Then: T1 leaves the list.
  • Set-aside expires, another hold waiting (INV-HTF-4)
    • Given: T1 is set aside for H1, and H2 is waiting
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: T1 is back on the list, with front hold H2.
  • Set-aside expires, no hold waiting (INV-HTF-4)
    • Given: T1 is set aside for H1, and no other hold is waiting
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: T1 is not on the list.
  • Set-aside past its collect-by date, not yet expired (INV-HTF-1)
    • Given: T1 is set aside for H1, collect by 17 October, and H2 is waiting
    • When: the list is read on 18 October, before Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: T1 is not on the list. It joins, with front hold H2, once Hold Expired lands.
  • Lapsed set-aside, next holder collects before expiry (INV-HTF-1, INV-HTF-4)
    • Given: T1 was set aside for Ben's H1, his collect-by date has passed, Cleo's H2 and Dan's H3 are waiting, and Cleo checked T1 out (ending H2) before Hold Expired was recorded for H1
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: T1 is not on the list: Cleo's loan is open. When Tool Returned is recorded for Cleo's loan, T1 joins the list with front hold H3.
  • Set-aside cancelled, another hold waiting (INV-HTF-4)
    • Given: T1 is set aside for H1, and H2 is waiting
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: T1 is back on the list, with front hold H2.
  • Set-aside holder closes their account (INV-HTF-4)
    • Given: T1 is set aside for Ben's H1, and Cleo's H2 is waiting
    • When: Close Account records Hold Cancelled for H1, because Ben closed his account
    • Then: T1 is back on the list, with front hold H2.
  • Front hold cancelled before it is fulfilled (INV-HTF-6)
    • Given: T1 is on the list, with front hold H1 and H2 behind it
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: T1 stays on the list, with front hold H2.
  • Last waiting hold cancelled (INV-HTF-6)
    • Given: T1 is on the list, with front hold H1 and no other hold
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: T1 leaves the list.
  • Front holder collects before the hold is fulfilled (INV-HTF-5)
    • Given: T1 is on the list, with front hold H1 (Ben) and H2 behind it
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for T1 and Ben, with Hold Collected for H1
    • Then: T1 leaves the list (the loan is open, and H1 is gone from the queue). H2 waits for T1's next return.
  • Tool retired (INV-HTF-7)
    • Given: T1 is on the list, with front hold H1
    • When: Retire Tool records Hold Cancelled for H1, with Tool Retired for T1
    • Then: T1 leaves the list.
  • Retired while on loan, then returned (INV-HTF-7)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan with H1 waiting, and the shed manager retired T1, which recorded Hold Cancelled for H1
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for Ana's loan
    • Then: T1 is not on the list.
  • Tool recorded lost while holds wait (INV-HTF-7)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan L1, and H1 is waiting on it
    • When: Record Tool Lost records Hold Cancelled for H1, with Tool Lost for L1
    • Then: H1 is gone, and T1 never joins the list.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-HTF-9)
    • Given: T1 is on the list once, with front hold H1
    • When: the same Tool Returned is applied again
    • Then: T1 is still on the list once, with front hold H1.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-HTF-9). An event applied a second time leaves the list as it was after the first.
  • Events for a hold that has ended: a later Hold Cancelled, Hold Expired or Hold Fulfilled for a hold that has already ended (a replay) changes nothing.
  • The fulfiller reads a tool twice before Hold Fulfilled lands: the list may return the same tool on two reads in a row. Fulfilling a hold only once, and only while the tool is still free, is Fulfill Hold's rule (INV-FUL-3), enforced when it records Hold Fulfilled; this list raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: read only by the Hold Fulfiller. No person or screen reads it.
  • PII & compliance: holds neighbor IDs only, no names or emails.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above. How soon after a return the tool is set aside is Fulfill Hold's concern.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, toolId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId (a loan is open).
    • Hold Collected (Collect Hold): holdId (the hold leaves the queue).
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId, toolId.
    • Hold Cancelled is also recorded by Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost and Close Account, one per hold they end.
    • These match slices/place-hold.md, slices/check-out-tool.md and slices/return-tool.md, and Hold Fulfilled as Fulfill Hold is being written. The others are specified in slices not yet written in depth; each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Fulfill Hold, whose fulfiller works from this list and records Hold Fulfilled.

Open Questions

None.

Slice: Fulfill Hold

Step 15 of 29 in Hold a tool for pickup · after Holds To Fulfill · before Tool Catalog — hold fulfilled · Automation

Intent

When a tool is back in the shed with holds waiting, set it aside for the neighbor at the front of the queue, so the tool goes to holders in the order they asked. The system does this itself; no person decides it. Returning a tool records only Tool Returned; Hold Fulfilled is recorded separately, by this slice.

What follows a fulfilment is decided by the slices that read Hold Fulfilled: the holder is emailed that the tool is ready (Send Pickup Notice, which doesn't hold up the fulfilment), My Holds shows it ready for pickup with its collect-by date, the Tool Catalog shows it set aside, and the set-aside lapses at the end of its collect-by date (Expire Hold).

Trigger & Actor

  • Pattern: automation. The Hold Fulfiller, a system processor, watches the Holds To Fulfill list (slices/holds-to-fulfill.md). No person fulfils holds; only the Hold Fulfiller issues Fulfill Hold, and it is not exposed to neighbors or the shed manager.
  • Triggering condition: a tool is on the list: it is in the shed, not set aside for anyone, and at least one hold on it is waiting. Each item names the tool, the hold at the front of its queue, and that hold's holder.
  • When it acts: the list changes only when an event lands (a return, an expiry, a cancellation, a closure), so the Hold Fulfiller acts whenever the list changes, on each item that appears.
  • What it does: it issues Fulfill Hold for the item's hold. If the command is refused or is a repeat, nothing is recorded and the processor moves on; the list will show the tool again with its new front hold, if there is one.

Command / Input

Command: Fulfill Hold

A HoldId is a UUID. One clock reading is taken when the command is handled. "Today" (for collectByDate) is that moment's calendar date in the shed's local time zone, and the event's fulfilledAt is that same moment.

FieldTypeRequiredRules / Validation
holdIdHoldIdyesThe hold to fulfil: the front waiting hold of its tool (INV-FUL-2). Must be a hold that has been placed (INV-FUL-9).

Trigger

Triggered by: processor Hold Fulfiller, also in this slice, reading Holds To Fulfill.

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Hold Fulfilled → context Holds Read by: Holds To Fulfill (the tool leaves the list), Tool Catalog (set aside), My Holds (ready for pickup), Pickup Notices To Send (the holder's email), Pickups To Expire (the collect-by date to watch), and Undelivered Notices (a later pickup-email failure's details).

FieldTypeImmutable Fact?Source / Notes
holdIdHoldIdyesFrom the command.
toolIdToolIdyesSet by the system: the tool on the hold's Hold Placed.
toolNameTextyesSet by the system: the tool's name on the hold's Hold Placed.
neighborIdNeighborIdyesSet by the system: the holder on the hold's Hold Placed.
neighborNameTextyesSet by the system: the holder's name on the hold's Hold Placed.
neighborEmailTextyesSet by the system: the holder's email current at fulfilment: Hold Placed.neighborEmail, replaced by any Neighbor Email Changed for the holder since.
collectByDateDateyesSet by the system: today plus 3 days. The set-aside lapses at the start of the day after it, shed local time.
fulfilledAtInstantyesSet by the system: the UTC moment the event is recorded.

collectByDate is recorded here once, so every reader uses the same date and none works it out.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. The Hold Fulfiller reads Holds To Fulfill, specified in slices/holds-to-fulfill.md. Hold Fulfilled takes the tool off that list and sets it aside in the Tool Catalog, My Holds and the pickup lists. All are eventually consistent: the list may still show a tool for a moment after it was fulfilled, which is why the command itself refuses a second fulfilment.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-FUL-2: A tool is set aside for the hold at the front of its queue: the hold, still waiting, whose Hold Placed was recorded first.
    • Queue order is the order the Hold Placed events were recorded, never a comparison of times.
  • INV-FUL-3: A hold is fulfilled only while the tool is in the shed and not set aside for anyone, and the hold is still waiting.
    • In the shed: no loan of the tool is open (Tool Checked Out without Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan), and it hasn't been retired.
    • Not set aside: no other hold on the tool has been fulfilled and not yet ended.
    • Still waiting: the hold hasn't been fulfilled and hasn't ended. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, the holder checks the tool out, the tool is retired or recorded lost, or the holder closes their account.
  • INV-FUL-4: A tool is set aside for one holder at a time.
    • A lapsed set-aside still counts until its Hold Expired is recorded. Only then is the next hold fulfilled.
  • INV-FUL-5: A fulfilled hold's collect-by date is the fulfilment date plus 3 days.
    • Until the end of that date, only the holder may check the tool out (Check Out Tool, INV-CHK-3). The holder collects it with an ordinary checkout.
  • INV-FUL-6: When a set-aside ends without the holder collecting it and another hold is waiting, the next hold is fulfilled in the same way.
    • A set-aside ends this way when the hold expires or is cancelled, or the holder closes their account. With no hold waiting, nothing is fulfilled and the tool becomes available.
  • INV-FUL-8: The front hold is fulfilled even if its holder can't collect right now, because they are suspended or have an overdue loan.
    • They keep their place. If they can't collect by the end of the collect-by date, the hold expires and the next hold is fulfilled.
  • INV-FUL-9: The hold must exist.
  • INV-FUL-10: Fulfilling a hold that is already fulfilled records nothing new.
    • A repeated request for that hold succeeds, so a list read twice never sets a tool aside twice or moves its collect-by date.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ben's hold H1 on the cordless drill was placed before Cara's hold H2. Today is 10 October in the shed's local time.

  • Happy path: tool returned with holds waiting (INV-FUL-2, INV-FUL-5)
    • Given: Ana returned the drill on 10 October. H1 and H2 are waiting, so the drill is on Holds To Fulfill with H1 at the front.
    • When: the Hold Fulfiller issues Fulfill Hold for H1
    • Then: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1: the drill, Ben, collect by 13 October.
  • Next hold after an expired set-aside (INV-FUL-6)
    • Given: the drill was set aside for Ben under H1, Hold Expired has been recorded for H1, and H2 is waiting
    • When: the Hold Fulfiller issues Fulfill Hold for H2
    • Then: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H2: the drill, Cara, collect by 13 October.
  • Next hold after a cancelled set-aside (INV-FUL-6)
    • Given: the drill was set aside for Ben under H1, Ben cancelled H1, and H2 is waiting
    • When: the Hold Fulfiller issues Fulfill Hold for H2
    • Then: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H2.
  • Next hold after the holder closes their account (INV-FUL-6)
    • Given: the drill was set aside for Ben under H1, Ben closed his account, and H2 is waiting
    • When: the Hold Fulfiller issues Fulfill Hold for H2
    • Then: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H2.
  • Front holder is suspended (INV-FUL-8)
    • Given: the drill is back in the shed with H1 at the front, and Ben is suspended
    • When: the Hold Fulfiller issues Fulfill Hold for H1
    • Then: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1: the drill, Ben, collect by 13 October.
  • Front holder has an overdue loan (INV-FUL-8)
    • Given: the drill is back in the shed with H1 at the front, and Ben has an overdue loan
    • When: the Hold Fulfiller issues Fulfill Hold for H1
    • Then: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1.
  • The list is read twice (INV-FUL-10)
    • Given: Hold Fulfilled has been recorded for H1, and the list showed the drill once more before it caught up
    • When: the Hold Fulfiller issues Fulfill Hold for H1 again
    • Then: the command succeeds and records nothing new. The collect-by date stays 13 October.
  • The holder collected first (INV-FUL-3)
    • Given: the drill came back with H1 at the front, and Ben checked it out before the Hold Fulfiller acted, which ended H1
    • When: the Hold Fulfiller issues Fulfill Hold for H1
    • Then: refused with hold-ended: "This hold has already ended." No event is recorded.
  • Not the front of the queue (INV-FUL-2)
    • Given: the drill is back in the shed with H1 and H2 waiting
    • When: a Fulfill Hold for H2 arrives
    • Then: refused with not-front-of-queue: "This hold isn't at the front of its tool's queue." No event is recorded.
  • Tool still set aside for someone else (INV-FUL-4)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben under H1, his collect-by date has passed, and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded for H1 yet. H2 is waiting.
    • When: a Fulfill Hold for H2 arrives
    • Then: refused with tool-set-aside: "This tool is already set aside for a holder." No event is recorded. Once Hold Expired is recorded for H1, H2 can be fulfilled.
  • Tool on loan (INV-FUL-3)
    • Given: the drill is on loan to Ana, and H1 is waiting
    • When: a Fulfill Hold for H1 arrives
    • Then: refused with tool-checked-out: "This tool is already checked out." No event is recorded.
  • Hold cancelled before the fulfiller acted (INV-FUL-3)
    • Given: the drill came back with H1 at the front, and Ben cancelled H1 before the Hold Fulfiller acted
    • When: a Fulfill Hold for H1 arrives
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded. The list shows the drill with H2 at the front.
  • Unknown hold (INV-FUL-9)
    • Given: no hold H9 has been placed
    • When: a Fulfill Hold for H9 arrives
    • Then: refused with hold-not-found: "There is no such hold." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

A refusal records nothing; the Hold Fulfiller logs it with the hold ID and moves on. No person sees these reasons. The name is the contract; the sentence is the log text.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. hold-not-found (INV-FUL-9).
  2. If Hold Fulfilled is already recorded for the hold, the command succeeds and records nothing (INV-FUL-10).
  3. hold-ended (INV-FUL-3).
  4. tool-checked-out (INV-FUL-3).
  5. tool-set-aside (INV-FUL-4).
  6. not-front-of-queue (INV-FUL-2).
ReasonSentenceRule
hold-not-foundThere is no such hold.INV-FUL-9
hold-endedThis hold has already ended.INV-FUL-3
tool-checked-outThis tool is already checked out.INV-FUL-3
tool-set-asideThis tool is already set aside for a holder.INV-FUL-4
not-front-of-queueThis hold isn't at the front of its tool's queue.INV-FUL-2

hold-not-found, hold-ended and tool-checked-out mean the same conditions as in Cancel Hold and Check Out Tool. A retired tool's holds have all ended, so a retired tool shows as hold-ended. A missing or malformed hold ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: a repeated Fulfill Hold for a hold already fulfilled succeeds and records nothing (INV-FUL-10).

Requests at the same moment: Fulfill Hold is decided against the tool's holds and loans as already recorded, one at a time per tool, so at most one hold on a tool is set aside at once. A holder's checkout, a cancellation or an expiry landing at the same moment is decided in the same order: whichever is recorded first stands.

There are no external calls in this slice. The pickup email is sent by Send Pickup Notice.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: Fulfill Hold is internal. Only the Hold Fulfiller issues it.
  • PII & compliance: Hold Fulfilled links a neighbor to a tool and a date. No name or email.
  • Performance / SLA: a tool is set aside within moments of the event that put it on the list. Nothing on record sets a tighter limit.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId. Queue order is the order these were recorded.
    • Hold Fulfilled (this slice): holdId, toolId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold), Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool), Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId, toolId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • The Hold Fulfiller reads Holds To Fulfill's items: toolId, holdId, neighborId (slices/holds-to-fulfill.md).
    • These keys match the deep-passed docs, and the Hold Fulfilled shape matches what undelivered-notices.md, check-out-tool.md and holds-to-fulfill.md read.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Holds To Fulfill, Tool Catalog, My Holds, Pickup Notices To Send, Pickups To Expire and Undelivered Notices. Check Out Tool reads collectByDate to enforce the holder's claim, and Expire Hold to find lapsed set-asides.

Open Questions

None.

Slice: My Holds

Step 2 of 29 in Hold a tool for pickup · after Place Hold · before Tool Catalog — hold placed · State View

Intent

Shows a neighbor the holds they have, on the My Holds screen: where they stand in each tool's queue, and when a tool has been set aside for them, the date to collect it by and whether the pickup email reached them. It is the only screen that tells a neighbor a tool is waiting for them, and the screen they cancel holds from.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: a neighbor, opening their own My Holds screen.
  • Whose holds it shows: the holds of the neighbor asking. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the neighbor's ID, resolving a person to their newest account, or to their closed one only when they have no newer.
  • Actions offered: nothing on this screen records anything by itself. Its one action issues a command owned by another slice:
    • Cancel (Cancel Hold slice) — offered on every listed hold (INV-MYHD-16).
    • A neighbor collects a set-aside tool with an ordinary checkout from the Tool Catalog, not from here.

Read Model / View

  • View: My Holds built from events: "Hold Placed", "Hold Collected", "Hold Cancelled", "Hold Fulfilled", "Pickup Notice Sent", "Pickup Notice Failed", "Hold Expired"
  • Consumed by: the My Holds screen (Neighbor)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events: a change shows shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Whether a set-aside's pickup window has ended is worked out when the view is read, from collectByDate and today's date in the shed's local time zone, so it is always current. No action on this screen depends on the view being instant, because Cancel Hold and Check Out Tool each check their own rules when they run.

One row per hold that hasn't ended. HoldId, ToolId, LoanId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be absent.

FieldTypeSource / Notes
holdIdHoldIdHold Placed.holdId.
neighborIdNeighborIdHold Placed.neighborId: the holder.
toolIdToolIdHold Placed.toolId.
toolNameTextHold Placed.toolName (INV-MYHD-14).
placedAtInstantHold Placed.placedAt. For display only; it doesn't decide the queue.
statusTextOne of waiting, ready-for-pickup, pickup-window-ended. Derived: see the status rules below.
positionIntDerived: while status is waiting, 1 plus the number of this tool's holds that are waiting, were placed before this one, and haven't ended (INV-MYHD-2). Optional: absent once the hold is fulfilled.
collectByDateDateDerived: Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate for this hold, read as recorded, never worked out here (INV-MYHD-3). Optional: absent while waiting.
pickupNoticeTextOne of none, sent, undelivered. Derived: sent once Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for this hold, undelivered once Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for it, none before either (INV-MYHD-13).
canCancelBoolDerived: yes on every listed hold (INV-MYHD-16).

Status rules. A hold's status is a test of its current facts, taken in this order. The first that holds wins:

  1. pickup-window-ended — Hold Fulfilled has been recorded for the hold, and today's date in the shed's local time zone is after its collectByDate (INV-MYHD-17).
  2. ready-for-pickup — otherwise, Hold Fulfilled has been recorded for the hold.
  3. waiting — otherwise.

When a hold leaves the view. A hold is listed from Hold Placed until it ends. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, or when the holder checks the tool out. In events:

  • Hold Cancelled or Hold Expired for the hold;
  • Hold Collected for the hold (the holder checked the tool out).

Retiring the tool, recording it lost and closing the holder's account each end holds by recording Hold Cancelled for them (Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost, Close Account). This view hears only the Holds events.

Queue order. A tool's queue is the order in which Hold Placed was recorded for it. To work out positions, the view keeps, for each tool, every hold on it that hasn't ended, with its holder and whether it has been fulfilled. This is bookkeeping, not part of the row, and other neighbors' holds are never returned.

Queries

  • List my holds. Takes the asking neighbor's neighborId. Returns every hold of that neighbor that hasn't ended, each with every field above, and nothing about anyone else's holds (INV-MYHD-1). There is no paging. A neighbor with no holds gets an empty list. Holds are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when the hold was placed, in the order Hold Placed was recorded (INV-MYHD-18).

Invariants / Business Rules

A neighbor has at most one hold on any one tool, because Place Hold refuses a second (INV-HOLD-7, Place Hold). A suspended neighbor can't place a new hold (INV-HOLD-9) or collect a set-aside tool (INV-CHK-7), but may still cancel. An expired hold sends no message, doesn't count against the neighbor, and the neighbor may place a new hold on the tool at the back of the queue (Expire Hold). A suspended neighbor keeps their holds and their place in each queue. A front holder who can't collect, because they are suspended or have an overdue loan, still has the tool set aside for them, and the pickup window runs regardless (Fulfill Hold, INV-FUL-8). These rules are owned by those slices; this view just reflects the events they record, and it doesn't hear suspension or loans at all (INV-MYHD-11).

  • INV-MYHD-1: A neighbor's My Holds shows only their own holds.
    • The query returns only holds whose holder is the neighbor ID it is given. It never shows who else holds a tool, only the neighbor's own position. No neighbor-facing screen ever shows who has a tool or who holds one; only the shed manager sees borrowers, on Tool Inventory.
  • INV-MYHD-2: Holds on a tool queue in the order they were placed. Each waiting hold shows the neighbor's position in that tool's queue.
    • Position 1 is the next hold to be fulfilled. A hold moves up as holds ahead of it are fulfilled or end.
    • A hold that has been fulfilled is no longer in the waiting queue, so the first waiting hold behind a set-aside is at position 1.
  • INV-MYHD-3: Once a neighbor's hold is fulfilled, My Holds shows the tool as ready for pickup, with the date to collect it by.
    • The collect-by date is the one Hold Fulfilled carries: the date the tool was set aside plus 3 days. My Holds shows it as recorded and never works it out itself.
    • My Holds is the only screen that tells a neighbor a tool is set aside for them. The Tool Catalog is the same for every neighbor.
  • INV-MYHD-4: A hold that is ready for pickup stays on My Holds until the holder collects it, cancels it, or Hold Expired is recorded for it. Then it drops off.
    • The tool then passes to the next hold, which shows as ready for pickup on that neighbor's My Holds once Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • INV-MYHD-5: When a holder checks out the tool they hold, their hold ends and drops off My Holds, whether or not it had been fulfilled.
    • The loan then appears on My Loans.
  • INV-MYHD-6: A cancelled hold drops off My Holds, whether it was waiting or ready for pickup.
    • Cancelling a hold that is ready for pickup passes the tool to the next hold, the same as expiry.
  • INV-MYHD-7: Retiring a tool, or recording it lost, ends every hold on it, and those holds drop off My Holds.
    • Retire Tool and Record Tool Lost record Hold Cancelled for each hold; this view hears those. The holders are not told.
  • INV-MYHD-8: Closing an account ends all of that neighbor's holds. Their holds drop off My Holds, and holds behind them move up.
    • Close Account records Hold Cancelled for each of the neighbor's holds; this view hears those.
    • A tool that was ready for pickup for them passes to the next hold, the same as expiry.
  • INV-MYHD-13: Once a tool is set aside for a neighbor, My Holds shows whether the pickup email was sent or couldn't be delivered.
    • If the email can't be delivered, the tool stays ready for pickup, with the same collect-by date.
  • INV-MYHD-14: Each hold shows the tool's name.
    • The name comes with Hold Placed, which carries it.
  • INV-MYHD-11: Only Hold Placed, Hold Collected, Hold Cancelled, Hold Fulfilled, Pickup Notice Sent, Pickup Notice Failed and Hold Expired change My Holds.
    • A checkout records Hold Collected only when the borrower had a hold on the tool; a checkout by anyone else is not heard here at all.
  • INV-MYHD-15: Applying the same event twice leaves My Holds as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-MYHD-16: My Holds offers Cancel on every hold it lists.
    • That includes holds ready for pickup, holds whose pickup window has ended, and holds of a suspended neighbor.
  • INV-MYHD-17: Once a set-aside's collect-by date has passed, My Holds shows that the pickup window has ended, even before Hold Expired is recorded.
    • From the start of the day after the collect-by date, in the shed's local time, the set-aside is no longer theirs: the tool goes to the next neighbor in the queue, or to whoever checks it out first if nobody is waiting (INV-CHK-3b, Check Out Tool). The hold drops off when Hold Expired is recorded.
  • INV-MYHD-18: Holds are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when they were placed.
  • INV-MYHD-19: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.
  • INV-MYHD-20: My Holds is answered only for the signed-in neighbor: a request for any other neighbor ID is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Hold placed (INV-MYHD-2, INV-MYHD-14, INV-MYHD-16)
    • Given: Ana has T1, the "Cordless drill", on loan, and nobody has a hold on it
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's hold H1 on T1, carrying the name "Cordless drill"
    • Then: Ben's My Holds lists H1: "Cordless drill", waiting, position 1, pickup notice none, with Cancel offered.
  • A second hold placed (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Cara's hold H2 on T1
    • Then: Cara's My Holds lists H2, waiting, position 2. Ben's is unchanged.
  • Holds placed in the same instant (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Cara's H2 and then Dan's H3 on T1, with the same placedAt
    • Then: H2 is at position 2 and H3 at position 3: the order recorded decides, not placedAt.
  • Hold cancelled (INV-MYHD-6, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Hold fulfilled (INV-MYHD-3, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1, and T1 has been returned
    • When: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1, with the collect-by date 17 October
    • Then: Ben's My Holds shows H1 ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, with no position. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Pickup email sent (INV-MYHD-13)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, pickup notice none
    • When: Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 shows pickup notice sent.
  • Pickup email couldn't be delivered (INV-MYHD-13)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, pickup notice sent
    • When: Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 shows pickup notice undelivered, still ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October.
  • Collect-by date is the last day (INV-MYHD-17)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October
    • When: his holds are listed at 23:59 on 17 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 is ready-for-pickup.
  • Pickup window ended, not yet expired (INV-MYHD-17, INV-MYHD-16)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded
    • When: his holds are listed at 00:00 on 18 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 shows pickup-window-ended, with Cancel still offered.
  • Hold expired (INV-MYHD-4)
    • Given: Ben's H1 shows pickup-window-ended, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 stays waiting at position 1 until Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • Suspended holder (INV-MYHD-3, INV-MYHD-11)
    • Given: Ben is suspended, and his H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: T1 is returned and Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1, collect by 17 October
    • Then: Ben's My Holds shows H1 ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October.
  • Holder collects the tool (INV-MYHD-5)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Collected is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's is unchanged.
  • Front holder collects before the set-aside is recorded (INV-MYHD-5, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1, and T1 has just been returned
    • When: Hold Collected is recorded for H1, before any Hold Fulfilled
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Ready-for-pickup hold cancelled (INV-MYHD-6)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 stays waiting until Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • Tool retired (INV-MYHD-7)
    • Given: Ben's H1 and Cara's H2 are on T1
    • When: Retire Tool records Hold Cancelled for H1 and for H2, with Tool Retired for T1
    • Then: H1 and H2 drop off both neighbors' My Holds.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-MYHD-7)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan as loan L1, and Ben's H1 and Cara's H2 are on T1
    • When: Record Tool Lost records Hold Cancelled for H1 and for H2, with Tool Lost for L1
    • Then: H1 and H2 drop off both neighbors' My Holds.
  • Holder closes their account (INV-MYHD-8)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1
    • When: Close Account records Hold Cancelled for H1, with Neighbor Account Closed for Ben
    • Then: H1 drops off. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Hold again after expiry (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 expired, and T1 is now set aside for Cara's H2
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's new hold H4 on T1
    • Then: Ben's My Holds lists H4, waiting, position 1, behind Cara's set-aside.
  • Only their own holds (INV-MYHD-1)
    • Given: Ben has H1 and Cara has H2, both on T1
    • When: Ben's holds are listed
    • Then: only H1 is returned, with its position. Nothing about H2 or Cara is returned.
  • List order (INV-MYHD-18)
    • Given: Ben placed H5 on the ladder, then H1 on the cordless drill
    • When: his holds are listed
    • Then: H1 (cordless drill) comes first, then H5 (ladder).
  • Same event applied twice (INV-MYHD-15)
    • Given: Ben's My Holds lists H1 at position 1
    • When: the same Hold Placed for H1 is applied again
    • Then: Ben's My Holds still lists H1 once, at position 1, and no later hold's position changes.
  • Not signed in (INV-MYHD-19)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: My Holds is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.
  • Asked by the wrong person (INV-MYHD-20)
    • Given: Ben (N2) is signed in
    • When: the holds of N1, Ana, are asked for
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only see your own holds." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

Reading this view is guarded like a command. A refused read returns nothing and one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown on the screen. The checks run in this order:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-MYHD-19).
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-MYHD-20).
ReasonSentenceRule
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-MYHD-19
requester-mismatchYou can only see your own holds.INV-MYHD-20
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-MYHD-15). An event applied a second time leaves the view as it was after the first.
  • Events for a hold that has ended: once a hold has ended it is gone from this view. A later event for it (a replay, or a Pickup Notice Failed that arrives after the set-aside ended) changes nothing.
  • Stale actions: Cancel offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, just as the hold expires or the tool is collected). Cancel Hold checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may list only their own holds (INV-MYHD-1). The query is always asked for the signed-in neighbor's own ID, which sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies; a request for any other neighbor ID is refused requester-mismatch (INV-MYHD-20), and one with no sign-in not-signed-in (INV-MYHD-19).
  • PII & compliance: shows a neighbor their own holds only, and never who else holds or has a tool. The other holders and borrowers it keeps for working out positions are never returned.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId, placedAt.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, collectByDate.
    • Pickup Notice Sent (Send Pickup Notice): holdId.
    • Pickup Notice Failed (Record Pickup Notice Failure): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Collected (Collect Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Cancelled is also recorded by Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost and Close Account, one per hold they end; this view can't tell those from a holder's own cancellation and needn't.
    • Hold Placed and Hold Collected match slices/place-hold.md and slices/check-out-tool.md. The others are specified in slices not yet written in depth; these keys are this view's assumptions, and each is checked when that slice is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Cancel Hold.

Open Questions

None.

Slice: Pickup Notices To Send

Step 18 of 29 in Hold a tool for pickup · after My Holds — hold fulfilled · before Send Pickup Notice · State View

Intent

The pickup notice gateway's to-do list: every tool set aside for a holder whose pickup email hasn't gone out yet, with everything the email needs. The gateway works through it, so each holder is emailed once, as soon as a tool is set aside for them.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the Pickup Notice Gateway, a system reaction in the Send Pickup Notice slice. No person reads this list, and it has no screen.
  • What the gateway does with it: for each hold on the list, it records Pickup Notice Sent, and the email is then handed to the provider keyed by the hold's ID (Send Pickup Notice slice).

Read Model / View

  • View: Pickup Notices To Send built from events: "Hold Fulfilled", "Hold Cancelled", "Hold Collected", "Neighbor Email Changed", "Pickup Notice Sent", "Hold Expired"
  • Consumed by: the Pickup Notice Gateway (Send Pickup Notice). Internal: no ui.
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. A hold joins the list shortly after Hold Fulfilled is recorded (seconds, not minutes), and leaves shortly after the event that ends it.

One row per hold on the list. HoldId, ToolId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

FieldTypeSource / Notes
holdIdHoldIdHold Fulfilled.holdId.
toolIdToolIdHold Fulfilled.toolId.
neighborIdNeighborIdHold Fulfilled.neighborId: the holder.
collectByDateDateHold Fulfilled.collectByDate, read as recorded.
holderNameTextHold Fulfilled.neighborName.
holderEmailTextDerived: Hold Fulfilled.neighborEmail, replaced by each later Neighbor Email Changed.email for that neighbor. Always the current one.
toolNameTextHold Fulfilled.toolName.

A row carries everything it needs from its own Hold Fulfilled; the view keeps no bookkeeping beyond its rows. Neighbor Email Changed updates the address on that neighbor's rows only.

When a row leaves the view. A hold's row is removed when, for that hold:

  • Pickup Notice Sent is recorded (INV-PNS-3);
  • Hold Cancelled or Hold Expired is recorded (retiring the tool or closing the holder's account records Hold Cancelled for it);
  • Hold Collected is recorded for the hold (INV-PNS-4).

Nothing puts it back.

Queries

  • List pickups to notify. Takes nothing. Returns every row, with every field above. There is no paging. The order doesn't matter to the gateway, which sends one email per hold.

Invariants / Business Rules

The list has no screen; only the pickup notice gateway reads it. When the email goes out, with no quiet hours, what it says, and that none goes out once the collect-by date has passed, are Send Pickup Notice's rules.

  • INV-PNS-1: A hold is on the list from the moment Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it until its pickup email is sent, or its set-aside ends first.
  • INV-PNS-2: Each item carries what the email needs: the holder's name and email, the tool's name, and the collect-by date.
    • The holder's name and email, the tool's name and the collect-by date are the ones Hold Fulfilled carries, read as recorded and never worked out here; a later Neighbor Email Changed replaces the email.
  • INV-PNS-3: Once Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for a hold, it leaves the list and never comes back.
  • INV-PNS-4: A hold leaves the list, unsent, when its set-aside ends first: the holder collects the tool, or the hold is cancelled or expires. Retiring the tool or closing the holder's account cancels the hold (Retire Tool, Close Account record Hold Cancelled).
    • A tool set aside for a holder is never on loan, so it is never recorded lost while on the list.
  • INV-PNS-7: Applying the same event twice leaves the list as if it had been applied once.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Set-aside joins the list (INV-PNS-1, INV-PNS-2)
    • Given: Ben Ito's (N2, ben@example.org) hold H1 is at the front of the queue for T1, the "Cordless drill"
    • When: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1, tool T1 "Cordless drill", holder N2 "Ben Ito", ben@example.org, collect by 17 October
    • Then: H1 is on the list with holderName "Ben Ito", holderEmail ben@example.org, toolName "Cordless drill" and collectByDate 17 October.
  • Pickup email sent (INV-PNS-3)
    • Given: H1 is on the list
    • When: Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 leaves the list, and never comes back.
  • Hold cancelled before the email (INV-PNS-4)
    • Given: H1 is on the list
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 leaves the list, unsent.
  • Hold expired before the email (INV-PNS-4)
    • Given: H1 is on the list
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 leaves the list, unsent.
  • Holder collects before the email (INV-PNS-4)
    • Given: H1, Ben's hold on T1, is on the list
    • When: Hold Collected is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 leaves the list, unsent.
  • Tool retired before the email (INV-PNS-4)
    • Given: H1, on T1, is on the list
    • When: Retire Tool records Hold Cancelled for H1, with Tool Retired for T1
    • Then: H1 leaves the list, unsent.
  • Holder closes their account before the email (INV-PNS-4)
    • Given: H1, Ben's hold, is on the list
    • When: Close Account records Hold Cancelled for H1, with Neighbor Account Closed for Ben
    • Then: H1 leaves the list, unsent.
  • Holder changes their email before the email goes out (INV-PNS-2)
    • Given: H1 is on the list with ben@example.org
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for Ben, to ben.ito@example.net
    • Then: H1 stays on the list, now with ben.ito@example.net, and the pickup email goes to that address.
  • No set-aside, nothing to send (INV-PNS-1)
    • Given: the list is empty
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Cleo's hold on a ladder
    • Then: the list is still empty.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-PNS-7)
    • Given: H1 is on the list once
    • When: the same Hold Fulfilled for H1 is applied again
    • Then: H1 is still on the list once.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-PNS-7). An event applied a second time leaves the list as it was after the first.
  • A failed pickup email: doesn't change the list. Every Pickup Notice Failed follows a Pickup Notice Sent, which already took the hold off the list, and this view doesn't hear Pickup Notice Failed.
  • Events for a hold that has left the list: a later event for it (a replay) changes nothing.
  • The gateway reads a hold twice before Pickup Notice Sent lands: the list may return the same hold on two reads in a row. Sending one email per hold is Send Pickup Notice's rule, enforced when it records Pickup Notice Sent; this list raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: read only by the Pickup Notice Gateway. No person or screen reads it.
  • PII & compliance: holds the name and current email of every registered neighbor, and hands them to the gateway only for holders with a tool set aside. It shows them on no screen.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above. How soon after a set-aside the email goes out is Send Pickup Notice's concern.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, toolId, toolName, neighborId, neighborName, neighborEmail, collectByDate.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Pickup Notice Sent (Send Pickup Notice): holdId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Collected (Collect Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Cancelled is also recorded by Retire Tool and Close Account, one per hold they end.
    • These match slices/add-tool.md, slices/register-neighbor.md, slices/change-email.md, slices/check-out-tool.md, and Hold Fulfilled as recorded in the conventions. The others are specified in slices not yet written in depth; each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Send Pickup Notice, whose gateway works from this list and records Pickup Notice Sent.

Open Questions

None.
